#3,507
Wandering Prince
Avatar the Last Airbender, Zuko SI
26
Commissioned by jblake.
After stopping by the castle for Toph to request a formal meeting for us, we checked into our hotel and paid for a week in advance. Then, we got settled in and spent some time cleaning up and washing off the road dirt. With nothing to do until the meeting but kill time, we decided to relax a bit first, then see the sights—something Toph was most eager for, as she'd be truly seeing them for the first time even though she'd been here before.

Shared baths had become the norm by now, so the girls wouldn't hear it when I suggested we separate. I personally just wanted some private time—a man has needs and it was hard to take care of those on the road, when one of your traveling companions could see what you were doing through the ground. Also, I figured the girls might want a break from me, or each other.

It turns out, I was wrong, and we spent most of the afternoon just soaking and sitting quietly, relaxing together in the hot water and just talking over a pot of tea. Afterwards, we took a short nap before heading out into the city as the sun set, allowing Toph to go out without her blindfold. For a while, we just explored, taking in the sights of this part of the city as Toph acted as our tour guide.

"It's pretty," the earthbender murmured, head turning this way and that as she tried to take in everything at once. "I remember there was a nice place my parents took us to, where we got food. I think it's this way."

It didn't take long before we found the place—a large, two story building that pretty much radiated wealth. I cast a glance at Toph. "Toph, how expensive was this place?"

"Uh," she hemmed, frowning. "I don't think anyone ever said. Actually, I don't remember ever hearing a number given. Pretty sure we own the place." Shrugging, she grinned and put an arm in Yue's, then marched forward, her stone shoes clacking on the stone path below us as she pulled the taller princess along. "Let's go find out!"

I got the door for the two ladies and followed them inside, where a man who looked to be in his twenties, wearing Earth Kingdom green and gold robes and standing at a podium near the door frowned upon taking us in. I was dressed fairly casually and playing the part of visible bodyguard, but the girls had done themselves up a bit—nothing too outrageous thankfully, but they definitely looked good. In other words, we didn't look like we were too poor to be in a place like this.

"Ladies, sir, I am afraid that the Flying Boar does not take walk-in guests off the street," he sent us a polite service smile that didn't reach past his lips. "If you would like to make a reservation, I would be happy to take your names and put you on our list. I believe we have a spot open some time next month."

Yeah, and I'm pretty sure that if we actually wait that long and come back, our reservation will unfortunately have been 'misplaced,' but we'll be able to reserve a spot for the next month. Rinse and repeat until we get the message.

Toph laughed, shaking her head and pulling out her papers. "Permanent reservation under Beifong."

The man frowned, before darting his hand out to snatch the papers. Toph pulled them back and slipped them back under her robe. "Where did you steal that from?"

"It's mine," Toph rolled her eyes. "I'm Toph Beifong."

The man scoffed. "If you're going to pretend to be related to the Beifong family, you shouldn't choose someone like the heiress to impersonate. She would never be here without her family, because she's blind. You are neither here with her family, nor do you appear to be visually impaired. Perhaps you should leave, before I call the city guard?"

The ground trembled slightly under our feet as Toph's eye began to twitch, her fists curling at her side. Yue winced, pulling her arm out of Toph's and putting it around her shoulder. "Come on, let's just go. There's no reason to escalate—"

Toph ignored Yue as the taller girl tried to pull her towards the door, locking her feet in place and becoming immobile. "Get me your boss."

"I won't be doing that. We don't trouble him with whatever rabble comes in off the street. Last chance. Leave, or I call the guard."

The shorter girl opened her mouth, only to yelp when I scooped her up and threw her over a shoulder. "Zuko! Put me down!"

"Hush," I warned her, smacking her ass beside my head for good measure. She fell silent and stilled, and I knew I'd probably pay for that one later. Looking to what I guessed was equivalent to some sort of maitre de/head waiter, I asked, "What was your name?"

"Worth more than the likes of you."

I nodded, message received. "Okay then. Girls, we're going."

I carried Toph out, Yue walking along beside us and closing the sliding door behind us. As soon as we were outside, a pair of hands grabbed my ass and squeezed. A sound like a yelp might have escaped as I dropped Toph, who landed on her feet with a laugh. "What was that for?"

"You started it," she snorted, taking a moment to straighten out her robe. "Ugh. That guy was an asshole!"

"Perhaps, but he wasn't necessarily wrong, either. It would be suspicious to see the blind heiress traveling alone and seemingly cured," Yue pointed out, to which Toph huffed.

"Don't care. We're stopping by and talking to the people running this branch of the business for my family. He's getting his ass busted back to bus boy. He'll be washing dishes for the next twenty years," Toph grumbled as I put a hand on her back and pushed her along, Yue on her other side, as we moved down the street.

"Let's just find somewhere else to eat and worry about it tomorrow," I chuckled, spotting what looked like a decent place just down the street and guiding Toph in that direction.

"How can you not be angry about this? You saw he looked down on us!" Toph complained, genuine upset in her voice.

"First time?" I asked, and she paused, before jerkily nodding. "If I took you two to my home and started throwing around who I was, I wouldn't be too surprised if someone eventually called bullshit, papers or no. And remember, we're trying to travel incognito. The only reason you get to flash that thing around right now is because it's convenient for getting us in to see Bumi. Don't get used to it. There are going to be places where the doors are just closed to us, without revealing who we are."

Toph made a frustrated sound, but slowly nodded. "Fine."

Rubbing her back, which caused her to lean into my side, I continued, "And a little petty revenge never hurt anyone. We can screw with this guy a bit officially, but in the future, you should limit yourself to small inconveniences."

Toph grinned. "I've got some experience with that," she chuckled.

"I almost feel bad for anyone who got on your bad side," Yue giggled as we made our way into what looked and smelled like some kind of deep fried food.

We enjoyed sharing our meals with each other, trading bits back and forth as we tried a bit of everything on each others' plates. Dessert was a light, cold tapioca pudding. We paid and left, walking around a bit to let our food settle, before making our way back to the hotel for the night.
The next morning, someone knocked at the door to our hotel as we were getting ready for the day. I cracked the door open to find a messenger wearing a guard uniform—though his was a bit different from those we'd seen around town. "Good morning. Can I help you…?"

"Is Ms. Beifong present?"

I turned and called, "Toph," waving her over. She came over and swapped places with me. After a quick conversation, he handed her a scroll and left. She turned back and grinned.

"Alright! We're going to see King Bumi!"

"When?" I asked, dropping into a seat on the room's one bed as Yue looked up from where she was still brushing out her bed hair.

"Just after lunch," she answered, waving the scroll, before tucking it up her sleeve.

"That's good news," Yue sighed. "We have a few hours before we need to be there. Can… can we go down and see the refugees?"

Toph and I traded a look, before the earthbender shrugged. I sent Yue a smile. "Sure. Just be careful. And keep an eye out for pickpockets."

Yue rolled her eyes. "I don't think they're going to steal from someone helping them."

Toph laughed out loud and Yue pouted, turning a hurt look on the shorter girl before looking at me. I shook my head and got up. "If we're ready, let's go. We'll go have a look around, then get lunch before we go see Bumi."

We left the hotel and made our way out into the city, backtracking to the district the gate guard had to avoid. The change was like night and day. Our surroundings went from a clean city obviously cared for by benders, with nice homes and businesses, hanging decorations, and strategically placed plants and flowers, to an area that was bare stone, rough, dirty, cracked buildings and streets, stinking of human waste, and even darker as it seemed to be in the shade of the other buildings around it and the exterior city wall, all sitting at a higher level. This place probably wasn't all that great or well cared for before, but now the streets were filled with beggars, homeless, people huddled close together or eyeing each other and us all warily.

Yue was undaunted, however, as she took the lead and pressed further down the shadowed street. Eventually we came to a square and she looked around. Turning to Toph, she asked, "Can you make us a little building?"

Nodding, Toph took a moment to turn the stone in part of the square over, grinding the filth away between layers of stone, before a simple square structure sprang up from the ground. Four walls, a roof, diamond shaped windows to let in light with stone slats, and a doorway and a sliding stone door made up the outside. Inside were benches for sitting in one room, while the other—accessed by a thin sliding stone door—had a bench and a waist high table just big enough for an adult to lie on. There were places for torches for lights in both rooms, empty for the moment.

"How's that?" Toph asked as we stepped inside and inspected it. "I've seen the inside of a few clinics. Well, not seen, but you know," she trailed off with a shrug.

Yue pulled the shorter girl into a hug. "It's perfect! Thank you."

We stepped back outside and Yue took a deep breath, before calling, "Everyone! I'm a waterbender," she opened her bending water skin and twirled water around her body to demonstrate. "If anyone is sick or has injuries that need tending, please come see me. I won't ask for anything in return!"

At the skeptical looks of those around, Toph quickly added, "But whatever you can give is fine!"

Yue sent a sharp look at Toph, but that seemed to set the crowd in the square more at ease and, a moment later, a young woman—maybe a few years older than us—approached. Quietly, she said, "I, on the road, I was…" Yue took her by the hand and led her inside with a soft smile, and we heard the interior door close.

"Looks like we're going to be here a while," I pointed out as people slowly began standing and warily approaching.

Toph sighed and stomped the ground, raising a porch around the front of the building and creating a bench against the outer wall. We took a seat and she pressed herself into my side, turning around and leaning back against me as she propped her feet up on the bench and rested her arms in her lap. Glancing back towards the people approaching, she called, "Form a line and state your problem. The healer will see you by how bad the problem is. If you're bleeding, something's broken, infected, or you've got a fever, front of the line."

The first to make it over was a man holding his stomach. I gave him a nod and asked, "What's wrong?"

"Got stabbed in the stomach by a bandit just before we made it into the city yesterday evening. It, it hurts bad. Bandaged it, but I don't feel great."

I bounced to my feet, causing Toph to squawk as she fell back onto the bench, and grabbed him by the shoulder, dragging him in. "Yue, drop what you're doing! Gut wound takes priority!"

"It's okay, I was just finishing up," Yue opened the door to the other room and the woman hurried out, blushing but wearing a smile. I pushed the man inside and Yue took over. "Please sit on the table."

"So… she's the real deal?" another woman in the crowd was asking the one who had just left.

I tuned out their conversation as the woman practically gushed over how Yue had helped her. Toph sat up and I took my seat again, and this time she dropped her head into my lap—apparently deciding I made a good pillow. I reached down and began idly petting her hair as another man came up with an obvious broken hand, looking swollen and purple.

"Can't work like this," he chuckled.

I nodded and jerked a thumb towards the door. "Go have a seat and wait your turn."

The next few hours passed by quickly as Yue took care of the worst of them. Until finally, the area brightened as the sun peeked out overhead—having gotten high enough to be seen between the wall and the other buildings. I gave Toph's head one final scratch before telling her, "Go get Yue, would you? We'll need to go soon. We can come back this evening if she wants."

Toph sighed. "But I'm comfy."

"And how's it gonna look if we're late to the meeting we scheduled, with the king?" I gently pointed out.

Toph blew out an annoyed sigh. "Yeah, okay, fine. …Pick this up later?"

I laughed. "Sure."

She beamed a happy smile and hopped up, making her way inside. "Yue! We need to go or we'll be late!"

"But, but I'm not done," Yue protested.

I could hear the eye roll in Toph's voice. "We can come back later."

Yue sighed, and a moment later I heard her apologizing to the people already waiting, before stepping outside. "Everyone! I'm sorry, but we have to go meet with King Bumi to try to get you some more help! I'll be back soon, though, I promise!" People looked disappointed, but it seemed most of them were willing to stick around and wait, as many of them just sat down where they had stood in line.

I stood and the three of us left, making our way out of the too narrow street with eyes on us the entire time—though this time, it felt like the attitude behind most of those gazes had changed, as they looked at Yue with hope, instead of looking at our entire group with suspicion. We hurried through the market district, stopping only long enough to get some barbecued skewers and tea for a quick lunch, before hoofing it to the castle.

Toph pulled the scroll she'd been given out of her sleeve and presented it at the gate. "Toph Beifong and friends to see King Bumi."

The guard took the scroll and looked it over, before nodding and gesturing for us to follow. "This way. I know I don't have to tell you Miss Beifong, but for the benefit of your guests, please mind your manners."

"Don't worry. Yue's a princess and Zuko is nobility. They do the 'manners' thing better than me," Toph grinned. "I'll probably say something dumb and get us in trouble. Maybe he wants to spar. It's been a while since I've had a good fight with an earthbender who doesn't suck."

"Please don't." Quieter, the guard added, "The king is very bored and everyone here either respects him too much to challenge him or is afraid of him, so he'll take any excuse he's given."

I reached out and laid a hand on Toph's shoulder. "Don't worry, we'll keep her out of trouble."

"As much as we can," Yue giggled on Toph's other side as the shorter girl grinned.

"That does not reassure me," the guard sighed.

Soon enough, we were shown to what looked to my eye like an audience hall. The door closed behind us and, looking around, I noticed a distinct lack of guards.

Then again, it's Bumi. He doesn't exactly need them, I mused as we made our way down the hall towards the throne, where an old man sat with a wide grin on his face. His hair and beard were wild and white with age and deep, purple bags were heavy under his eyes—but those eyes were still a bright green that held a calculating, intelligent gaze. For all that he looked like someone's doddering old grandfather, the one who just didn't give a fuck anymore so would say whatever was on his mind but half the time that mind was stuck fifty years in the past… that was a ruse. He might be a bit off, but all of his faculties were clearly still intact.

Beside me, Toph looked more uncomfortable the closer we got. Turning a look on her, I asked, "You okay?"

"The old fart's trying to collapse the ground under us and I'm fighting against it. And if he doesn't stop, I'm gonna knock him off that throne!" Toph growled the last loud enough for the old man in question to hear.

Bumi laughed, slapping his knee, and Toph relaxed as whatever he was doing apparently stopped. "An earthbender, a waterbender, and a firebender walk into a bar…"

"They should've ducked," I answered reflexively, and the old man laughed harder.

Sighing, Toph reached up and pulled off her blindfold. "Wow. I can finally see your ugly face and I kind of wish I couldn't."

"That's no way to talk to your elders," Bumi glared at her, but there was little heat in it. "So what happened? Got your eyes fixed and your parents were still trying to kept you wrapped in cotton?"

"Kind of the other way around," Toph admitted. "I made some friends. Took over the Earth Rumble in Gaoling. Found out my parents were planning to marry me off and hold onto the family business while waiting for our kids to get old enough to take over, cause they don't trust me to run it. So I ran away. We're on vacation."

"Mm. And are you going to introduce me to your friends, or keep being rude?" Bumi asked, raising an eyebrow.

"I can do both, you senile old coot," Toph snorted.

"Toph!" Yue gasped, going wide-eyed. "She didn't mean that—"

Bumi laughed again and I sighed. "Don't bother, Yue. We've been played." I turned a look on Toph, to find her grinning up at me. "It's obvious these two have met in a less formal setting before."

"Well, it was kinda hard to hide what I was doing when we visited. He figured out I was an earthbender and was using the ground to sense pretty quick. I picked up a few tricks when we visited and have been working on them since."

"She was a precocious little brat sneaking out of her hotel when her parents went to sleep so she could go run scams on the local criminal element!" Bumi grinned. "I was ready to step in and keep 'em from roughing her up, when the reality was, I almost needed to step in to keep her from roughing them up too much!"

Yue's eyes narrowed into a glare at Toph. "So you were playing a prank on us?"

"Yep!" the little gremlin leered.

"We can get her back later," I assured Yue.

"Anyway!" Toph clapped. "These are Yue and Zuko. She's the princess of the Northern Water Tribe and he's—"

"Prince Zuko," Bumi nodded, and I raised an eyebrow. "What? I'm old, not senile. And your country likes to brag. They announced it the day you and your sister were born, and you're just old enough to be him. Besides, you look like Iroh when he was younger."

"Of course you've met Uncle," I sighed, and the old man nodded. "Lemme guess, if we play a game of Pai Sho, you'll probably kick my ass unless I open with the white lotus."

"Why don't we get out a board and find out, young man? It's been a while since I've played anyone who hasn't just let me win."

I shrugged. "Sure. We can do that later if you like. Before that though, we did come here for a reason," I said, before looking to Yue and sending her an encouraging smile.

Biting her lip, Yue nodded and stepped forward, bowing deeply at the waist. "King Bumi, we come before you seeking aid. Not for ourselves, but for your people!"

"Hoh?" he asked, reaching up and stroking his beard. "And what sort of aid would that be?"

"I'm sure that by now you're aware of the refugees coming to Omashu," Yue continued. "These are just the first of many! There is a line of people from villages that have been looted, pillaged, and burned by pirates marching here this very moment, from all up and down the coast. From nearly as far south as Gaoling. They have little, and what little they have is taken from them by bandits harassing them on the roads. Those that make it here are tired, hungry, sick, wounded, and many of the women have been assaulted. Many of your people are going to die if they don't get help soon!"

Bumi sighed, slumping in his throne as his jovial attitude fell away. "Oh please do stand up straight. I hate it when people bow," he grumbled, waving a hand at Yue. Shifting his gaze to Toph, he asked, "All the way to Gaoling, huh?"

"Pretty much. We've seen it ourselves. There have to be thousands of them. It seems like every village on the coast has been hit. The entire coast is just a line of smoke from burning villages," Toph confirmed. She stomped a foot and a bench rose up behind us. She dropped into a seat and Yue and I followed. "We met Zuko's Uncle and it seems like the Fire Nation are aware and sending ships to help, because a lot of those villages are mixed, but we've got no idea how many ships we're talking about and, well…"

"My people aren't exactly welcome in the Earth Kingdom," I finished for her. "So even if they showed up with material aid, chances are most people who weren't already from those Fire Nation settlements are going to turn it down. There's definitely a fleet in the area, since they tend to patrol the Fire Nation port cities on the coast to make sure those don't get raided, but there's a chance that they've just pulled in to defend those and decided that Earth Kingdom villages are an Earth Kingdom problem."

"Mm," Bumi hummed, stroking his beard again. "It's worse than I thought. I sent runners to determine how bad it was and they seemed to believe we were nearing the end of them."

"There are large gaps between some of the groups," Yue supplied. "But I promise, there are a hundred times as many coming as have already arrived. Omashu will be drowned in a flood of people if something isn't done."

"Yes, and we don't want that," Bumi mused. "There aren't enough supplies for that many people, even if I tap into the city's reserves. That many sick and wounded people crammed so closely together, sickness is sure to take root and spread among them like wildfire, then into the rest of the city. Not to mention, we just don't have the room for that many people in the city. We're on a mountaintop you know! Space is limited, unless we start digging down and expanding."

Leaning back in his throne, he frowned, crossing his arms as he thought it over. "The problem is, even if I dispatch people to bring relief and take care of the bandits, the pirates are still a problem. I don't like the idea relying only on the Fire Navy to handle them—as you said, there's every chance they won't."

"If you can't do anything about them, then don't," I suggested. "Focus on what you can deal with. It seems to me like this is a problem that can be solved with manpower, instead of just throwing money or resources at it and hoping it sorts itself out."

The old man grinned. "Oh? Let's hear it then. How would you handle it, if you were sitting where I am?"

I nodded. "This is the Earth Kingdom. You've got a surplus of earthbenders, right? Even just here in Omashu, you've probably got a few hundred who aren't part of the guard. Why not offer work? See who wants to volunteer to go help. Offer decent pay. They go out with a few guards and intercept the refugees. Most of them are just fishermen—no benders in their number, or they could've stopped the pirates. Build a simple village for them. Maybe help them gather some supplies so they can start rebuilding their boats that were stolen or burned. If you send teams like that, you can leapfrog them. One team stops to help one group, one team moves on further down the coast and helps the next. The first team finishes, passes by the second team, stops the next group, repeats the process, and so on. Deal with any bandits they come across along the way, of course. Make sure the villages are walled off and harder for pirates to assault. It solves the issue of refugees swarming Omashu, takes care of the bandit trouble, makes it harder for pirates to raid them in the future, and earns you the goodwill of basically everyone on the coast."

"And am I supposed to feed and clothe all of them too?" Bumi asked, raising an eyebrow.

Toph spoke up before I could. "The Beifong family will help provide relief. I'll speak with our local branch and send a letter off to my parents, but I'm the heiress and I'm here now, so I can make the call. We'll provide material and food aid and see if we can source carpenters and other skilled workers to help. In exchange, and in lieu of payment, we will require guards for our supply caravans providing that relief and will expect some benefits in the future. One thing I know my parents have been complaining about are taxes. Some sort of permanent decrease in taxes would be ideal."

Yue and I blinked, looking at Toph like she'd just grown a second head. Reaching out, Yue placed a hand on Toph's forehead. "Are you okay?"

"Huh?" Toph asked, confused.

I forced myself to keep a straight face as I asked, "Who are you and what have you done with our lovable idiot?"

Toph sighed, rolling her eyes as she elbowed me in the side and pushed Yue's hand away. "Shut up~. Just because I enjoy smashing my problems, doesn't mean I can't use my brain!"

"Okay, it's her," Yue sighed, smiling.

Bumi spoke up before we could devolve into bickering and/or flirting. "Well, if you can manage that much, I'll approve it and send people out. I'll need it in writing."

"Right," Toph straightened, nodding. "I'll have my people draw up a formal contract and leave the right spaces empty so we can fill in what we need to. It'll probably take a day or two."

Bumi nodded. "It will take that long at least to work through all the political nonsense involved in mobilizing a relief effort and convincing them that the information is good. Though, I have to ask, if you've seen miles of them coming as you've said, and yet you're here before all but the second wave… How did you get here this quickly, from Gaoling? Even taking a ship would have taken more time, and the raiding didn't start that long ago."

The three of us exchanged looks. Yue looked pensive, while Toph simply shrugged, deciding to leave it up to me. Nodding, I sent Bumi a grin. "Funny story, that. We actually sent another group of refugees this way ourselves, not long ago—but they haven't made it here yet and won't for a while. The short version is that a very smart man invented a means of traveling through the air. He was being held prisoner by the Fire Nation and being forced to develop weapons for them. I helped him complete the design, so he built a prototype for himself and his people to flee, and helped build a second one for me and Yue. We have a ship that lets us fly. It runs off of coal and the same sort of boiler engine Fire Nation ships use, but instead of using propellers to move water, they move air. It's very fast and lets us fly over forests and mountains, or along coasts."

Bumi's mouth fell open for a moment, before he laughed. "I'd love to see it. But I think that if you brought it here, my advisors would work behind my back to take it and turn it over to Ba Sing Se, to turn the tide of the war effort. Well then, I just won't mention that part. I'll tell them you came in with the latest trade caravan." Nodding to himself, he looked to Toph. "If you'll go put your foot in your people's butts and get them moving on this, I'll do the same."

Toph popped up and Yue and I quickly followed. "Alright! We'll be back once we've got something hammered out, old man!"

"I'll let the guards know to expect you," he confirmed.

"Ah," Yue spoke up, and our gazes turned towards her. "One other thing?"

"Yes? What is it?" Bumi asked.

"We built a little clinic in the lower district, where I've been treating patients. Is that okay?"

"Certainly! By all means, if you want to help, the land and the space is yours for as long as you want them. If you'd like, I can arrange to have guards accompany you and make sure things stay civil."

Yue hemmed, then shook her head. "I don't think that's necessary. They're already skittish of strangers and I think guards would do more to keep them away. I'll be fine with Zuko and Toph. Thank you, King Bumi."

"You're quite welcome. If there's anything you need for that clinic, don't hesitate to ask. I'll make it happen."

Yue nodded and when we left, it was with a huge smile on her face. We stepped out of the castle into sunlight and she turned her smile on us. "I'll go back to the clinic and get to work while you handle things on Toph's end."

"It's fine, I can take care of it," Toph shook her head, giving me a push in Yue's direction. "Go with her and I'll catch up."

"I'll be fine," Yue rolled her eyes. "I think they'll be more comfortable if it's just me. Please?"

Toph and I exchanged a knowing look, before I sighed and nodded. "Alright. Go on ahead. I'll go with Toph and we'll come by when we're done."

"Thank you!" Yue beamed, before turning and hurrying away.

Toph waited until she was out of earshot before asking, "You're not really letting her go alone, are you?"

I scoffed. "Fuck no. You got this?"

"I'm good," she nodded. "Go watch our princess and make sure no one tries to put their filthy hands on her."

"'Our princess,' huh?" I teased, and Toph blushed, glaring.

"Shut uuup~! Go!" she pouted, turning away and stomping off.

I laughed and followed after Yue, slipping into an alley and making my way onto the rooftops where I could observe covertly.

#3,561
Wandering Prince
Avatar the Last Airbender, Zuko SI
27
Commissioned by jblake.
Pai Sho pieces clacked on the board as Bumi and I played. Across from me, the old man scratched at his white hair, glaring at the board. Finally, he grumbled, "What has that old fart been teaching you?"

"This is actually one of Yue's maneuvers. Surprised me the first time I saw it, too," I chuckled, laying down another piece and claiming yet another of his.

"It's rude is what it is!" he complained, fumbling as he attempted to mount a defense against the tide sweeping across the board—to no avail.

It was slow to set up, but once it got going, the tsunami would sweep the board and there was little the other player could do about it for a direct counter, unless they themselves started with the same strategy. Of course, there was still an element of luck involved, so it wasn't a guaranteed win—but so far, numerically, it had won against nearly every strategy we'd tested it against. I wasn't a master however, so I was pretty sure someone had thought of it before and there was a counter to be had, as with everything when it came to this game.

Still, in this particular instance, Bumi didn't have such a counter and eventually found his pieces swept off the board entirely. Finally, the old man sighed and sat back, nodding to himself as he looked over the board's final state. "So, you'll be leaving us soon."

I nodded, reaching over and collecting my cup of tea to take a sip—a bit of fire heating it back up to the proper temperature. "Tomorrow. We've done what we came here to do. More than, even. You're aware of the situation. You're dispatching help. The Beifong family's company is going to help. We've done about all we can reasonably do. And as much as I'd love to stick around a while, this place is getting kind of crowded and I'm getting that urge to move on."

Bumi hummed, nodding along. "You've done more than enough already. This is my responsibility, as king of this region. One day, you'll bear that responsibility yourself."

"Not today," I sent him a smile. "Did you learn what was going on with the pirates? This seems a bit excessive, right?"

The old man eyed me speculatively for a moment before nodding. "One of my patrols captured and interrogated a boatload of them as they were coming in to raid a village, a few days ago. A messenger only just arrived this morning, carrying the news and what was said. Apparently, someone burned down one of the largest pirate trading ports on the coast.

"There was a bit of a fight over what to do afterwards and one firebender came out on top. A woman. She declared herself a pirate king or some such. She has one of your navy's cruisers and a crew of firebenders working for her, and the report said that the pirates believe she is a former Fire Nation naval officer turned pirate. They've taken over an island and turned it into a stronghold, and are building themselves a raiding fleet by press-ganging benders into service, in addition to all the other not so nice things they've been up to."

"Murder, theft, slaving, rape. The usual," I muttered, and Bumi nodded.

"Yes. And with an island of their own, you could say they're becoming a Pirate Nation. Just what the world needed."

Well… Yue's not going to like that. Question is, do I break it to her myself, or not? I've been kind of waiting for an 'I told you so' moment to come around, but this is a bit outside the scope of what I was expecting. Bit bigger than I'd feared it'd get, really. Not really doing her any favors by not telling her. She needs to see that actions have consequences.

That's not to say that I'm not just as culpable here. I made the call to burn the place. We could have left it, but I decided to kick the hornet's nest. Damn. I'm going to have to do something about it. Something more permanent than burning their shit and scattering them.

"Is there anything you can do?" I asked, and Bumi hummed.

"I could send word to Ba Sing Se. Unfortunately, the Earth Kingdom doesn't have much in the way of a navy, as you know. It's the Fire Nation who rule the seas," he shook his head. "I don't believe we'll be able to confront this so-called 'pirate king' directly." Eyeing me with an amused grin, he continued, "If only there were some way of getting this information to the Fire Nation. Certainly, being an island nation, a pirate fleet is as much or more of a threat to them…"

I chuckled, nodding. "I'll talk to Uncle and get him to send word." Sighing, I stood and stretched, popping my back as I did. "And on that note, I should get going. I'd like to get our stuff packed and head out at first light in the morning." Sending him a curious look, I asked, "So, did you make a decision about my offer?"

Bumi hummed, once more stroking his beard. "I'll need some more time to contemplate it, and perhaps speak with the others."

"That's fine," I nodded. "The offer will stand as long as it can. I've already made my point, but I'll say it again: we could use your help when the time comes, and having your current experience and power on top of having your youth back would tip the scales."

The old man sent me an amused look, nodding as he did. "I'll keep it in mind. Safe travels. Oh, and Zuko?" he asked, and I sent him a questioning look. "If you find Aang, send him my way, would you?"

"Will do," I agreed.

Leaving the castle, I made my way towards Yue's clinic. It was starting to get dark, and Yue tended to wrap up around now, so I wasn't terribly surprised to meet her and Toph on their way out of the side street out to meet me.

"So, how did it go?" I asked as I steered us towards a street vendor to get a quick bite to eat.

"Slow," Toph grunted, leaning over and thumping against my side as we walked. "Boring."

"It was fine," Yue rolled her eyes at Toph's complaint. "Mostly minor stuff. It looks like we got the worst of it before it got too bad. But there's a lot of other things. These people were starving and on the verge of death. Their bodies were weakened, so a lot of them are starting to get sick in the new environment, and it's beginning to spread in such close proximity, so I'm starting to see a lot of fevers. And then there are all the women…"

Yue fell silent as we got our food and found a nice place to sit down with an unobstructed view over the mountains to the west, where the last sliver of sun was starting to dip below the mountains. We ate in silence for a few moments before I looked to Toph. "Any last minute problems out of your family's company?"

"Nope," she shook her head. "It helps that the deal Bumi offered was really good. It's set up to keep going once we leave. They'll send word back to my parents with a note from me." Reaching up, she pulled off her blindfold—now down to the last few layers and thin enough that I could make out her eyes through it when she wore it. Sending me a smile, she thumped my arm with her fist, before turning her smile on Yue as well. "Thanks for that, by the way."

"You don't have to—" I started, only for the girl to cut me off.

"No, I do. You gave me something no one else could," she shook her head. "Both of you."

Yue's smile was soft as she reached out and laid a hand on Toph's. "You are very welcome. We're happy to have you as our friend. That's all the thanks we need."

Toph blushed and a sound escaped her throat as she turned away. "Nn, it's so embarrassing when you say things like that," she muttered. "And I can't even be mad 'cause I know you mean it." Turning desperate green eyes on me, she gestured at Yue frantically, "How do you deal with this?!"

"Lately?" I asked, turning a grin on Yue, who perked up and giggled. "Usually with affection. Kissing her at least gets her to stop for a minute."

Toph turned a contemplative look on Yue, who simply smiled and raised an eyebrow in challenge—daring Toph to follow through. The shorter girl shook her head and turned her attention back to her food, looking defeated for the moment. Chewing a big mouthful of saucy chicken, she worked things around in her mouth enough to ask, "What about you? Talk to Bumi?"

"Ah. Yeah," I nodded. "I'd wanted to hold off on this. It's kind of a mood killer. Let's just spend our last night here enjoying ourselves?"

Yue blinked, blue eyes going wide. "We're leaving? Already? But we've only been here a few days! There are still so many people left to help, and if I go now, everyone is going to get sick!"

I sighed, taking a moment to sip at my tea and think. As I did, Toph's good cheer fell off and she frowned as she looked between me and Yue, but she kept silent. Eventually, I decided I'd just tell them what I learned. "Bumi's going to be sending his people out soon. Within the week. Between them and the Beifong family, things are pretty much handled here. But King Bumi gave me some information before I left. Apparently, some of his people captured some pirates as they were trying a raid and interrogated them. The pirates that call these waters home have a new leader. A pirate king. Rumor has it she's former Fire Navy and she has one of our cruisers. They're organizing and building themselves up a fort on an island, since someone torched their largest base on the mainland. That's what kicked all this off and gave this woman an opportunity to step in, take over, and force them to work together instead of as just a bunch of separate pirate groups."

Yue frowned, picking up her tea cup and staring into it in silence as she thought. It was Toph who asked, "Didn't you tell me you're the ones who…" Yue flinched and I nodded. "Oh. And you just let those guys go, so—" Another flinch from Yue. "Ooh."

"It's my fault​."

I studied Yue's face as she closed her eyes, fingers clenching the stone cup tightly. "I chose to kick the hornet's nest. I'm equally to blame."

Yue shook her head, white hair from her bangs falling into her face. "No. You were right. We couldn't just leave them. You wanted to finish the job and I, I couldn't stomach it."

"Why is that? I don't get it," Toph sighed, eyeing Yue with confusion. "Your people dealt with pirates more than pretty much anyone. It had to be a weekly thing, at least. They attack your ships and you guys handle them like everyone else does. You have to know that! So why not—"

"Because they're still people!" Yue snapped, cutting Toph off, looking up from where her tea had abruptly frozen over, the cup cracking in her hands. She winced and set it down. She lowered her voice and her tone softened as she continued.

"They're just people. Normal men and women who have fallen on hard times. Why do you think so many people turn to becoming bandits or pirates? One year, the catch is slim, or there's a drought and they can't harvest enough, and they don't have enough to feed themselves, pay taxes, and trade. A lot of those little villages are just barely scraping by. A bit of bad weather, a migration in whatever animals or fish they take in, could be the difference between being able to put food on the table and watching their children slowly starve! They look at their neighbors, who had a good catch, or a good harvest, and they feel the world isn't fair. That they're being singled out and punished for no reason. They get jealous, and angry. That's when they decide to just… take what they need.

"That's how bandits and pirates are made. Just normal people, taking what they need from others, because they're hungry and the other kingdoms are threatening to take everything they own to pay for taxes that they see no benefit for, to fund a stupid war that should have ended a hundred years ago! It's not right to just kill them, because they're leaving behind families that rely on them to bring in food, and it's not just a single life you're ending!"

When she finished, Yue was left panting and red faced, her eyes wet with unshed tears as she glared between me and Toph. Toph frowned, looking over and meeting my gaze. I sighed and nodded. Reaching out, I grabbed the last chicken skewer off of her plate. "Give me that, I'm hungry."

"Hey! Give it back!" Toph glared, pouting up at me as I took a bite.

"Nope. And I'll kick your ass if you try to take it."

Crossing her arms over her chest, Toph pretended to sulk for a moment, before looking at Yue's plate. Reaching out, she took the last skewer off of Yue's plate for herself. "I'm hungry, give me that!"

Yue blinked, frowning as she reached up and wiped her eyes. "Huh? That's mine? I was still eating it," she protested.

"Don't care. Starve," Toph shrugged, stuffing her face.

Yue groaned and made to stand. "I'll go buy some more—"

"Nope. Give me all your money, too," Toph demanded, holding out a hand. "And if you wanna go grow a chicken, I'll be back to take that when it's done. Only way I'm stopping is if you kick my ass, but if you let me go, I'm coming back with friends and we'll fuck you up."

Yue sat back down as I took the extra skewer off of my own plate and put it on hers. Crossing her arms over her chest, she pouted. "It's not that simple."

""It really is,"" Toph and I countered at the same time.

Toph picked up from there. "Look, I get it. Family business. I know how the markets work and what it takes to put food on the table and in the market," she waved the partly eaten skewer in Yue's general direction. "It's hard to predict the weather. Taxes suck. The war sucks. Pests suck. Blight sucks. Bandits and pirates stealing your crap sucks. And when that happens, you work harder! You find some way to make it work! Go out and fish, or hunt, plant more crops, move away somewhere without the problems you had, or maybe prepare for shit happening ahead of time so that you don't go hungry in the first place! But you know what you don't do when something bad happens outside of your control? You don't go spread the misery by stealing someone else's stuff! You don't kidnap, enslave, rape, and murder people!"

Yue looked away as Toph glared at her across the table. "They're still people—"

"They're not," Toph shook her head, and Yue's head snapped up to glare at her. "You know what locusts are?"

Frowning, Yue shook her head. "No?"

"It's a bug. It eats crops. Some years, we get a lot of them and they swarm. They go from town to town, flying across the countryside and eating everything in their path. They don't care that by eating all of your crops, you might starve. They've got a family to feed. They're just looking out for themselves and their family. Pirates and bandits are the same. They don't care that you'll suffer, they're going to take everything you have because they want it. They're locusts on two feet. And you know what we do with locusts? Same thing we do with bandits and pirates."

"What about their families?" Yue demanded, and Toph shrugged.

"They're probably gonna die, yeah. And that sucks too. But it's not our problem. They should've convinced their husbands or whatever not to be criminals."

Sighing, the waterbender slumped in on herself. "I don't like it."

"Yeah, I get that," Toph nodded. "But which do you like less? The thought of killing criminals, or killing, raping, enslaving, and hurting innocent people?"

"That's not—"

"It is, Yue," I sighed. "As a ruler, you have a choice. Do something about the problem or let it spread and hurt innocents. Doing nothing, letting the problem get worse, is the same as condemning those innocents to whatever fate pirates or whoever had in store for them. You're saying you value the lives of the worst sort of people, who have chosen to make their living making others suffer, over the lives of the innocent citizens under your responsibility. Is that the kind of ruler you want to be?" Quietly, I said, "It's not the kind I want to be."

"There has to be another way," Yue shook her head.

Toph held up a hand and began counting off points on her fingers. "Kill 'em, solve the problem permanently. Jail 'em, have to put money into taking care of them, they might escape and go back to it. Enslave 'em and make them work off what they've done, same problems as jail. Cripple 'em, they become a burden on everyone around them, and you've pretty much just guaranteed them a slow death. Punish 'em, whip them, beat them, something—that just makes them angrier and they'll take it out on the next person they attack. Exile 'em, make them someone else's problem, but that just means they'll go cause problems for someone else, or they could come back later. Or like Zuko said, do nothing, which is the same as saying you support what they're doing and throwing everyone else in your country under the cart. That's really it. All those options suck, yeah. So you've gotta pick the one that sucks least, for the fewest people."

Yue turned to me for help but I shook my head. "If there were some alternative where everyone came out happy, don't you think someone would've figured it out by now? You could argue that it's a problem of not enough resources and money to go around, but look at Ba Sing Se. Richest city in the world. There are still criminals doing the same things bandits and pirates do. You could argue it's because those resources aren't evenly distributed, but then you get into the problem of telling the farmer that his work every day raising crops is just as valuable as the bum doing nothing but drinking all day, and he's going to have to share equally with everyone, including the bum—and that's going to make the farmer not want to farm. Why would he if he could do nothing and the government would give him just as much food and money as he was when he was farming? No one will work if there's no incentive to and they're given what they need to survive, until there's no one left to farm and no food left to go around. A country can't sustain itself like that."

"This… sucks," Yue blew out an explosive sigh, and I nodded.

"Yep," Toph sighed, finishing off the last of her skewer. "So… hotel, pack up, and head out at first light?"

"Yeah," I agreed, standing up and gathering my trash to throw away.

Yue was slower to follow and silent the rest of the way back. She stayed that way, sulking quietly, as we took a quick scrub and bath, then went to bed—where she was more clingy than usual, but otherwise looked to be in thought.

The next morning, we got up early and dressed. Yue placed a hand on her pack and stared at it for a few moments, before sitting on the bed as Toph and I started for the door. Turning back, I sent her a questioning look. "You okay?"

"No," Yue shook her head.

"Well, come on. If we hurry, we can grab breakfast before the lines start, then be out the gate and on the road before the crowd," Toph gestured towards the door impatiently.

Yue chuckled quietly, shaking her head again. "I'm staying."

"You're staying?" I repeated, and she nodded.

"What?! Why?" Toph demanded, dropping her pack. For a moment, the usually confident girl looked unsure. Quietly, she asked, "Is it about what I said last night? Look… I wasn't trying to be mean—"

"No! No, it's not that," Yue shook her head, before glaring mildly at Toph. "You were a little mean, but," she sighed, "I understand why."

"So then why?" Toph asked, crossing her arms over her chest and pouting.

"I've been thinking about it since we decided to come here. Then, when we got here and I started helping people… I knew then. I knew this was my fault, but I didn't want to admit it. These people are here because of me. I can help them, and I owe them that much."

Considering her words, I asked, "How long?"

Yue sent me a small smile and shrugged. "As long as it takes."

"I'm not going to be able to talk you out of it, am I?"

Yue shook her head. "I'm sorry." Sending me a smile, she asked, "I can't convince you to stay, can I?"

I shook my head. "There are things I need to do. Places I need to go."

Taking a breath, Yue bit her lip and admitted, "I still want to see the world with you. Both of you. And everything that comes after. But this is where I'm needed now. And I know you feel responsible too, right?" she asked, and I nodded. "I don't want to be there for that. So… go. Do what you need to, and I'll do what I need to here. Then, when we're both ready," she reached up and fingered the red silk of the choker holding her engagement pendant, "we'll travel together again."

"This is so duuumb," Toph groaned. "You're really gonna just stay here?"

"Mhmm," Yue nodded. Toph opened her mouth and she said, "Go with Zuko."

"Someone should stay with you," Toph murmured.

Yue smiled. "Toph," the earthbender looked up, green eyes meeting blue, "I'll be fine. Go. Enjoy your adventure."

Toph blew out an annoyed sigh and turned a look on me. "I'll go talk to my people if you'll talk to Bumi. We can at least make sure the hotel's paid for, she has what she needs for the clinic, and he's got a guard with her, right?"

"I don't need a guard," Yue rolled her eyes, but we both ignored her.

I dropped my pack by the door. "We'll be back in a few. Let's have breakfast together before we go."

Yue nodded, standing and following us out. "I'll get us food. Meet back here?"

We agreed and split up as we left the hotel. Thankfully, despite the early hour, people here were early risers. I was let in to see Bumi and explain the situation within a few minutes of arriving. For some reason, he didn't seem too surprised.

"You don't look surprised."

Bumi chuckled. "Zuko my boy, I knew the moment she asked for help. Can you honestly stand there and tell me you're surprised?"

"No," I admitted. "I suppose not. It's been brewing for a while now. I knew, eventually, her soft heart would get the better of her. It's why I love her, but it's also…"

"Frustrating?" the old man grinned, and I nodded.

"Yeah, a bit. I like that she wants to see the best in people, and doesn't want to settle for 'good enough' if there's a better answer, but…"

"But wide-eyed optimism, hope, and trust, as wonderful as they are, must be tempered by reality and experience," Bumi murmured, his grin falling off. "It is a hard lesson to learn and not one you can teach. It must be learned the hard way." The man sighed, and for the first time, he truly looked old. Before, he seemed like a man young at heart who just happened to be approaching the end of his years. Now, the weight of age and experience hard won truly showed. "She reminds me of myself, when I was a child. Back before the war began. And if she is to be a ruler of her people," he eyed me with a grin, "or wed the future Fire Lord," I nodded, confirming his guess, "then she needs that tempering."

"You'll make sure she's safe?"

Bumi nodded, waving a hand dismissively, "Of course! As safe as can be, at any rate. I'll assign a couple of guards to make sure no one causes her trouble. While she's helping my people, I'll make sure she's taken care of. She'll be paid every week and I'll speak to the owner of the hotel where you're staying and keep the room reserved for her until you return."

"Thanks, Bumi," I sent the old man a smile and he grinned.

"Think nothing of it, lad. Now, don't keep that girl waiting. For the heart to grow fonder, there must first be absence, you know?" he laughed, waving me towards the door.

I nodded and left him there, making my way back to the hotel, where I found Toph and Yue waiting, sitting around the room's low table with a breakfast spread between them. I took off my boots and joined them. Toph sent me a raised eyebrow. "Well?"

"I let Bumi know." Looking to Yue, I explained, "He'll be paying you weekly and you can stay in the hotel for free. He's also assigning guards."

"I don't need guards," she sighed.

"Well, you're going to have them." Her eyes met mine and she held my gaze, before eventually giving up as she realized I wasn't going to budge on this.

"Great. I talked to my people. Whatever supplies you need, they'll get," Toph added, picking up her chopsticks and digging in.

Yue likewise began eating, but not before sending us both a grateful look. "Thank you both. I know this was a bit sudden, and, and I know you don't agree with it. So thank you, for understanding."

Toph frowned, stabbing at her food a bit harder than was necessary. "Yeah, well, you'd better be ready to go when we come back," she grumbled. Looking up, she added, "Don't be mad if I steal a march!"

Yue laughed, shaking her head. "I won't be mad. A little jealous, but not mad."

"If everything goes to plan," I paused, then rapped the wooden table once just in case, "then it could be a few months. Maybe a year. Maybe a little more. We'll meet up with Uncle, then visit the library."

We could really use a waterbender for the desert, but we would have to make do with a few barrels of water. Either way, we weren't staying in the desert long. Of course, thinking on it, Yue did a lot for us and we'd have to adjust to not having a waterbender handy. That was going to suck.

"From there, maybe a stop or two before we head to wherever the Avatar might be, assuming Aang is still alive. Recruit him, bring him back, and we'll have a waterbending teacher waiting for us here," I raised an eyebrow at Yue, who smiled and nodded. "Then we can start preparing to deal with my father and put an end to this war, for good."

All too soon, breakfast came to an end. We found ourselves reluctant to part, but someone had to make a move or we never would. So, I stood and Toph and Yue followed. Yue pulled Toph into a tight hug that Toph returned, hard enough to pop something in Yue's back from the sound of it.

"Gonna miss you," Toph murmured into Yue's chest, earning a nod from the taller girl.

"Me too. Take care of each other," she whispered, kissing the top of Toph's head.

"Take care of yourself," Toph demanded, and Yue nodded.

They let go and Yue eyed me hesitantly. I pulled her into a hug and she darted in, her lips finding mine. When we broke the kiss, she pressed her face into the crook of my neck. "Stay safe."

"You too. Be careful."

"I will," Yue nodded. Taking a breath, she quietly said, "There's so much I want to say…"

"Save it for when we see each other again," I told her, and she nodded.

We kissed again before I let her go, taking the pack Toph offered me. "We'll see you soon."

"Mm. Soon," Yue nodded, biting her lip as she watched us leave.

The door closed behind us and Toph made an annoyed noise as we left the room and the hotel behind. Bumping her shoulder into me, she said, "This blows."

"A bit," I agreed. "Want to go kill some pirates?"

"Fuck yes," she chuckled.

"We can't sink the boats, you know," I pointed out, and she pouted. "They belong to those fishermen. We should take them back once we secure them."

"Ugh, fine," Toph grumbled as we hurried through the street towards the gate. "And since we're gonna be over water, I can't exactly just pull stone out of the earth."

"You'll need to bring some with you," I confirmed.

She hummed. "Rock armor?"

"Bulky. You fall in unconscious, you're going straight to the bottom. Maybe if someone worked on her metalbending more…"

Toph grumbled, but nodded. "Let's stop and buy some scrap iron. I'm sure there's a smithy or two with some we can use for me to make a weapon or something."

We made a quick stop to do exactly that, before hitting the road out of Omashu. We walked until sunset, with Toph making sure we weren't being followed, before stepping off the road and setting up camp. The next morning, we made our way down through the valley and up to where we'd left the airship.

Toph sat beside me as I took us up that night, looking out over the moonlit scenery. "It's just not the same."

"No, it's really not," I agreed.

"Think she'll be okay?"

I considered it for a moment before nodding. "If push comes to shove, I think so."

Leaning against me, Toph yawned. "Wonder what she's doing."

"Probably going to bed."

"Ha ha. You know what I mean."

Chuckling, I put an arm around the girl as she shivered. "Probably making friends over some bleeding heart sob story."

"Right? We'll come back and she'll have the city eating out of her hand because she's the one kissing their booboos better," Toph rolled her eyes. After a moment of thought, she asked, "…What if some guy hits on her?"

I laughed. "I don't think I have anything to worry about."

"You say that now, but you know… what if he's hot? And a bad boy?"

I pinched her side and Toph squirmed, elbowing me in response. "As the prince of the Fire Nation, I'm pretty sure that has me at the top of the list of 'bad boys.' There are none badder."

"Mm, true~," Toph murmured.

"Besides, have you seen this face?" I asked, pointing to the face in question. She turned and looked up at me, nodding. "I'm just too pretty to lose that battle."

Toph laughed, shoving me lightly. "Shut up!"
"Next please," Yue called, after sending her latest visitor on their way. A moment later, the door to the back room opened and a young man stepped in. He was about Zuko's age and height, with a square jaw, tan skin, dark eyes, and a mop of brown hair that was cute in that messy way. A pair of swords were belted to his hips and a piece of grass dangled from the corner of his mouth.

"How can I help you?" Yue asked, sending him a smile.

The man rolled up his sleeve and held out his arm, showing a bloody bandage wrapped around his forearm. "Well doc, I got this cut training."

Yue nodded, patting the table, and the man hopped up onto it. "Please, call me Yue. Now, let me see."

"Name's Jet."

It had taken a few days of flying from Omashu to the coast, then heading down the coast to find Uncle. True to plan, they had hugged the coast, just over the horizon from land, and circled the peninsula on the southwestern side of the continent, where Chin Village was located, and were currently steaming for the north towards Omashu, intending to patrol the coast for pirates.

After rendezvousing with Uncle and letting him know what Bumi had decided, and that Yue had chosen to stay behind and help, we parted ways again. Uncle's ship would patrol the coast and go to officially send word to the rest of the Fire Navy about the Pirate King and her taking over of an island, while with the advantage of a much faster airship and the increased visual range it offered, we would scout for the island they had taken over and pick off individual pirate ships as we encountered them. Uncle had a few ideas as to who it could be from his time in the service, but he couldn't be certain so he had only warned me to stay away from her if we found her.

Since we were close, and it was on my list of places to visit, I'd swung us south in search of Kyoshi Island. And now, it seemed we'd found it—almost straight south of Chin Village by a bit over a hundred miles.

"That's it?" Toph asked, as we looked down at the island some distance ahead and below us. The island was fairly large, with several small villages around the outskirts and towards the center, with a larger town and a large manor directly in the middle of the island. There were a few candle lights or the lights of fires inside homes barely visible in the dark, but it seemed most of the island had retired for the night. We were running under full blackout up here, so from below we would be little more than a silhouette against the night sky.

"Seems so," I agreed, sweeping the island with my spyglass. It looked like they had been raided and taken some damage. I spotted a few homes and buildings which had been burned down entirely in the smaller outlying villages, but it looked like most of the villages were intact.

"What's the plan?" Toph asked, leaning against my side.

Closing the scope, I set it aside and began working the controls, slowly losing altitude and bringing us in to land on the southwest side of the island, in a crescent shaped cove with a long, sandy beach. From the air, it looked like an almost perfect circle had been punched out of the tip of the island. In fact, looking closer, I was almost certain that was exactly what had happened—probably at the hands of some earthbender.

"Land and tie the boat off, then we'll make camp for the night. In the morning, we can do our usual morning workout, then head inland and start asking about the pirates. See if anyone knows which way they went after they hit the island, or if they were able to burn down the ship or ships that showed up. Offer some help if they need it." Reaching out, I put an arm around her and gave her a squeeze. "We'll make do. It'll give you an opportunity to find a way to use earthbending in new ways. Working with water may help you with the whole 'earth as water' aspect as well."

Suki yawned as she rolled out of bed and pulled on a robe, then stumbled into her kitchen. Moving the embers of last night's fire around, she quickly built up a new fire and put on a kettle to heat. After a quick stop to use the restroom and clean up after the night's sleep, then a trip out to one of the henhouses with a basket to collect fresh eggs, she made her way back inside and started rousing her sisters out of their beds.

"Rise and shine, Kyoshi Warriors~!" she called, laughing as she jerked sheets off, to protests from the other girls.

"It's not even dawn!"

"Five more minutes!"

"Go away, Suki! I don't have the energy for you right now."

"Unless you've got breakfast ready, I'm not getting out of bed."

Chuckling, Suki made her way into the kitchen and put the frying pan over the fire, then started on eggs, some leftover ham from a pig that had been slaughtered recently, and a bit of rice from last night's meal mixed in. By the time the girls were up and dressed, she had five plates of breakfast ready at the low table and had started pouring tea. The girls joined her a few moments later and they quickly began to eat.

"What are we doing today?"

"Same thing as yesterday, probably. Duh."

Suki held in a sigh and shook her head. "For now, the same as we have since the attack. Head home in the afternoon, then we'll train before bed."

"And the villagers?"

"Deal with your own wounds first, before trying to help anyone else," Suki reminded. There were some annoyed faces at that, but the girls understood. As much as they'd like to go hunt down the pirate scum that had taken their people, they first needed to make sure there were no more pirates lurking on the island to cause trouble.

Once breakfast was finished, chores were quickly divided amongst them and they went about preparing for the day. Dishes were washed and put away. A second meal was cooked and put away in bento boxes. A pot of tea poured into bamboo thermoses. Then they got dressed and got their armor and makeup on. Lunch was put away in their bags.

The sliding door closed behind them and the girls began their quick march from their little village to the highest point on the island. There was a moist chill to the pre-dawn air and a silence to the village that Suki enjoyed. Only the very earliest of risers was even just getting up at this time, as the roosters started to crow.

The girls were quiet as they marched up the trail to the top of the mountain, eyes sweeping the trail and their surroundings in the almost gray light. Their footsteps fell silently, occasionally crunching on a loose rock here and there, but always quiet enough that if someone had moved close to the village in the night they were sure to slip up on them.

Finally, they reached the summit, and the old lookout tower. It was both a fire watch tower and a makeshift lighthouse with a brazier that one of the local families had the duty of keeping lit at night. These days though, it had begun seeing more use from the girls as somewhere to scout the island from.

In the early days after the first pirate ship landed, they had taken to scouting from here to look for ships or fires on the island. Many pirates were buried in shallow graves, tossed into the sea, or fed to the farmers' pigs because they hadn't realized the danger the Kyoshi Warriors posed to them and people were predictable.

Everyone enjoyed a hot meal, and cooking food meant either starting a fire the old fashioned way, or having a firebender heat things up. But the thing about pirates was, those who were benders tended to act like they were above the common rabble of non-bender pirates, from Suki and the girls' covert observations of them. That meant they never used their bending for such mundane tasks as cooking. The girls climbed the tower and lowered the cover onto the brazier to snuff it out. Looking out over the island, Suki took a moment to enjoy the sight of the island as the sun began to slowly rise in the east. Focusing on what was in front of her, she took in everything to the south, all the way down to Koi Bay. Light glinted off of something on the beach and she spotted the light of a fire, but no smoke.

"Girls," she murmured, drawing their attention and pointing. "Who has the spyglass?"

Commissioned by telsiree.
I dropped Toph onto her feet as I landed and we sprinted into the forest. Glancing back, I saw the dust kicked up by Toph's smoke screen settling and the Kyoshi Warriors getting their bearings. I brought us to a stop and crouched, Toph doing the same beside me as we watched.

"Why aren't they coming after us?" she asked, frowning as the girls on the beach talked among themselves.

"Old hunter's trick. When you shoot an animal, if it doesn't drop right away, it's going to panic and run. That fear and will to survive is going to drive it to go way further than it would have otherwise, long after it should have bled out and collapsed. So you wait. Give it five or ten minutes. Then you track it, slowly. Quietly. Eventually, the fear fades and all that's left is the pain, and being tired from the sudden flight while fighting against their wounds. The animal will slow, then eventually lay down somewhere and usually pass out from blood loss and die. But if at any point it thinks you're pursuing, it'll get right back up with a new dose of fear and keep running. And that could go on for days. I've made that mistake before and it's never fun trying to run one down."

"That's what they're doing? Waiting for us to get tired, think we lost them, and slow down to take a break?"

The girl in the net stopped her struggling. Sighing, she asked, "I don't suppose you'd be willing to let me go?"

"Ask your leader," I sent her a smile.

"Uhh… Sure. Just don't tell her how I got caught?" she asked uncertainly, and I nodded.

"If you behave. Otherwise, I'll tell her just how embarrassing this was for you. Until then, we're going to tie you up with your friend so you can't go anywhere or give away the game. So… we gonna do this the easy way or the hard way?"

The Kyoshi girl nodded, gesturing at Toph. "See! She gets it!"

He chuckled and shook his head. "But we don't want to leave. Not yet. But I'm getting to that. As for you all, you're the Kyoshi Warriors. The last of Avatar Kyoshi's own personally trained, what? Honor guard?"

Suki nodded as she pushed aside a vine dipping into her path. "Yes."

That's just a huge, overcomplicated mess and a headache for everyone, and wastes time and energy that would be better spent solving the actual issue at hand. That being, the pirates."

Put down the sword, take off the makeup, leave the Kyoshi Warrior thing at the door and I'll do the same for the prince and my own sword. Then it's just two people talking as equals."

'They hid under your fat ass, Suki!'

'I'm surprised you didn't suffocate them, Suki!'

'One of your natto farts and they'd have begged to surrender, Suki!'

"Alright. We're in. What's the plan?"
