If it is as large as we hope, then the wisest course would be to liberate the island first. If we are lucky, it will still be overhead when we reach the island and we can take the northern port, then move on to secure the others, before attacking the city in the center of the island."

I returned to my seat between Toph and Suki and asked what I felt was the obvious question. "What do we do with the prisoners, once we've dealt with the pirates?"

"Mm. A difficult question," Uncle murmured. Glancing up at Suki, he sent her a smile. "Kyoshi Island is on the way to Gaoling. It is a small detour and will only cost us a few hours. We have food and water, and plenty of unoccupied beds on the ship, and what food and water we don't have we can take from the pirates when we free the island."

Blinking, Suki asked, "You would do that for us?"

"Of course," Uncle nodded, sending her a look as though the answer should be obvious. "It is the right thing to do."

"And the others?" I asked.

"Obviously, we cannot transport everyone," he shook his head. "However, there are sure to be some among the prisoners familiar with sailing. Once we remove the threat of the pirates, they can use those ships to return home. Once we see those from Kyoshi home, we will go after the pirates targeting Gaoling."

Toph let out a frustrated breath of air, before nodding once. "Fine."

Looking at Toph, Suki offered, "Once our people are back and we confirm that the pirate base and the main pirate force has been eliminated, Kyoshi Island won't need as many people guarding it. If you give us a few hours, we can try to round up some volunteers."

"That slows down the ship—" Toph started, only for Suki to cut her off.

"We'll take Zuko's," Suki spoke over her. "This ship drops everyone off then gets back on course for Gaoling. You and Zuko come with us to explain everything to Oyaji. My girls and I will head to the villages and ask for volunteers. Then once we've got everyone, we can fly back to the ship and drop them off, before moving ahead to scout for the pirate ships."

"She's going to be slower with more people. We're already losing forty knots with all of the new modifications and you girls," I pointed out.

"…Did he just call us fat?"

"He did!"

"Zuko why?!"

"It's Suki. All the weight is in her chest."

"You sure it's not in your ass?

"No, it's definitely Suki. Let's throw her overboard!"

"Hang on, we still need her as a life preserver."

"I kept saying it looked like she was giving herself larger portions than everyone else."

"Quiet!" Suki growled at her sisters, glaring at the other four as her hands clenched and unclenched in her lap, as though she was imagining wringing their necks.

A knock at the door interrupted our discussion and a moment later, the familiar form of the captain entered. He paused for a moment upon seeing the painted and robed forms of the Kyoshi girls, but quickly brushed it off and saluted Uncle. "Sir."

"Ah, captain. We need to change course." Uncle reached out and tapped the arrowhead shaped island on my map. "This is our destination. Your best possible speed. We should make landfall on the northern tip of the island. Tell the men to expect combat."

The captain nodded. "Yes, sir. I'll make sure we're ready."

"Also," Uncle continued before he could leave. "We are expecting to take on guests, once the fighting is done. We'll be transporting some people to Kyoshi Island on our way to Gaoling, to intercept a pirate fleet. Zuko, how many ships did you say?"

I thought back to the journal with the schedule. "At least eight large ships, maybe twice as many smaller ones. It wasn't a small fleet."

The captain frowned. "We're handling them the usual way?"

Iroh nodded. "Yes. That is why it's imperative we reach them before they can take prisoners."

"Understood. I'll get us under way. Excuse me," the captain gave another salute and hurried from the room, closing the hatch behind him.

"Now, we wait. More tea?" Uncle asked, offering the teapot up and refilling cups as the girls held theirs out. Sending Suki a smile, he asked, "Tell me, do you play Pai Sho?"

Suki sent him an innocent look as her sisters hid smiles behind their hands. "I dabble here and there."

"Excellent! Zuko! Go get the Pai Sho set from my quarters!" Uncle grinned and I rolled my eyes, pushing myself to my feet and leaving the room to track it down. As I left, I heard him ask Toph, "So, what has happened since I last saw you and my nephew?"

"Not much," Toph answered, and I heard the grin in her voice. "We beat up some girls on an island—"

"Hey! They didn't beat us up!"

"No, they tied us up~."

"Getting tied up and gagged like that… I think I awakened a new fetish!"

"We promised we weren't going to talk about that!"

"You promised. We didn't!"
Azula panted as she pushed herself harder, running through another drill. Her body ached, shaking with exertion and dripping with sweat. Her spirit itself protested as she demanded more, breathing in and trying to gulp down as much chi as she could from the air.

Feeling the wisps of energy spread from her lungs through her body, she stepped through the form, looking within herself and separating the chi. Positive chi flowed to her right arm and negative to her left as she swung her arms around.

Shoving what little was left out in front of her, Azula watched as positive chi met negative and an arc of lightning flashed, briefly connecting her and her target. But it was thin. Anemic. It barely left a burn mark on the straw target's chest, where before she had burned fist sized holes through them.

Azula's vision went blurry and the world swirled around her. Her knees felt weak and her heart hammered in her chest. She felt empty—drained entirely of chi and even emotion as a strange sense of calm settled over her, all of the emotions she fueled her bending with burned up as fuel. Her stomach rumbled and she felt so hungry it left her feeling sick, and so thirsty that she felt like she could drink the entire turtle-duck pond.

Just before she would have allowed herself to collapse onto her back, close her eyes, and just rest for a few minutes to recover, a voice from nearby drew her attention.

"Azula~!"

Azula did not groan at the sound of Ty Lee's voice, but it was a near thing. Through sheer stubborn will, she forced herself to stand up straighter and open her eyes, made them focus on the two girls approaching her in the garden where she had been practicing. "Ty Lee. Mai. Welcome back," she managed to get out, before frowning as she took in the lack of her brother with them. She narrowed her eyes and opened her mouth, only for Ty Lee to sweep her into a hug.

"We missed you too!" the handsy, entirely too energetic girl squeezed her, and Azula stumbled, nearly falling over if it weren't for the other girl holding her upright. Making a face as she pulled away, Ty Lee grinned. "You're all sweaty. Mai! Let's go take a bath together~!"

Sighing, Mai nodded and moved up on Azula's other side as Ty Lee wordlessly held onto her, supporting her weight and mostly dragging her towards the baths. "Fine. It'll give us time to talk."

As they passed a servant in the hall, Azula looked at the older woman and ordered, "Have food and something to drink brought to the bath. And a fresh change of clothes!"

"Yes, princess," the woman bowed her head and scurried off as they continued on down the hall.

Soon enough, Azula was stripped, washed clean with Ty Lee's help, and seated in the hot water to let her muscles loosen up between the only two people she considered friends. Closing her eyes, she yawned and rested her head back against the lip of the bath as they waited for the servant to return with food.

Thankfully, it didn't take long for the woman to return, carrying a tray of food over top of a folded bundle of clothes. She put the clothes away where Azula could find them later, before bringing the tray over and placing it down on the edge of the tub. "Will there be anything else, princess?"

"Thank you. And no, that's all. You can go," Azula waved the woman towards the door and listened as her footsteps pattered across the tiled bathroom floor. Only once the door opened and closed again did she crack her eyes open and try to force herself to move, only for Mai's hand on her shoulder to stop her. She sent the taller girl a brief glare as Ty Lee pushed her way through the water and got to the food first.

Ty Lee took a moment to pour three cups of tea and load a plate down with food, before carrying it all through the water and stopping in front of Azula and Mai, who took the offered cups. Popping a rice ball into her mouth whole, Ty Lee chewed and swallowed as Azula bit into her own with much more decorum, despite how utterly ravenous she felt.

Quietly, the princess asked, "Well? Where is he?"

Mai answered, loudly enough that Azula knew the servants (and likely spies) listening in would definitely hear it. "We caught up to Zuko in a little village in the Earth Kingdom. He said to tell you that he's not returning from his voluntary self-exile until he restores his lost honor and worth in your father's eyes by hunting down the Avatar."

For just a moment, Azula felt a flash of anger return as the coals her emotions had burned down to had fresh fuel thrown on top of them. The water warmed around her, fresh steam wafting off of it as she burned off the dregs of chi she'd recovered. The woozy feeling returned and she reined in her emotions and chi, glaring at her two friends.

Internally however, things she had noticed came together to form a picture she didn't like. Zuko's absence. Mai's blatant pitching of her voice for anyone listening to hear. The absolute crock of shit that was the cockamamie story about the Avatar.

It was readily apparent that her friends were lying to her. The question was, why.

Azula knew that others could find her hard to deal with at times, thanks to her brother's repeated warnings on the subject that if she wasn't careful she'd wind up pushing away the only two girls willing to tolerate her. She didn't think it was so bad that they would lie to her face though. At least, not out of malice or spite.

Which means it's something else. And the only other thing that would convince them to lie to me like this, and be so blatant about it, would be Zuko. He told them to lie. Why?

"You've failed me," Azula hissed angrily, crossing her arms over her chest.

"Ehehehe~!" Ty Lee laughed, sticking out her tongue. "Sorry Azula~! He really didn't wanna come back!"

"Were you born this incompetent or did you train at it?" the princess spat, turning away and storming out of the bath. "I should have never trusted this to someone else. I'll go find him and drag him back myself! Tell me you at least know where he's going."

"We do," Mai answered as she quickly got out as well, hurrying to grab a towel as Ty Lee scrambled out behind her.

Ty Lee put the plate and cups down and hurried across the bathroom, grabbing a towel before Azula could and starting to work on drying the angry princess off. She would never say it, but Azula appreciated the effort, since she couldn't muster enough chi to flash dry herself at the moment—she was pretty sure she'd pass out and fall flat on her face if she tried.

"Well, where's he going?" Azula demanded as she held her arms out and let Ty Lee work.

"To check the old air temples for signs of the Avatar. We know which order he's visiting them in, so we can meet him at the next one," Mai explained, but Azula had a feeling that was a lie for the benefit of any listeners.

"Fine! We'll have the ship you used resupplied, then we'll go after him. We're leaving tomorrow, as soon as they're ready," Azula nodded, and from outside, she heard the faint sound of feet hurrying away down the hall.

Shrugging Ty Lee's hands off of her, Azula hurried to grab her clothes. Still damp, she pulled them on as the others got dressed. Pulling her damp hair back, she tied it into a loose tail and, as soon as they were ready, led them out of the palace—sticking to the hidden passages and routes that would keep them away from prying eyes. She didn't bother stopping by her room to collect anything, or letting her father know—he would only slow her down and ensure his spies went with them.

Instead, as soon as she was out of the palace, she led her friends through the city down to the docks as quickly as she could without running. After traveling in silence for some time, Ty Lee finally asked, "Are we in that big a hurry?"

"We are if we want to go without father's eyes and ears following and reporting our every move back to the palace," Azula grumbled.

Eventually, they made it to the dock and Mai pointed out their ship. The girls hurried aboard and Azula made her way to the bridge, where they found the captain looking over a journal, with only one other crewman on the bridge that Azula mentally dismissed. The man frowned as they entered, then snapped to attention upon recognizing Azula. "Princess. How can I be of service?"

Azula smirked. That was what she liked to hear.

"We need to be ready to depart within the hour."

"Within the hour?" he repeated, sending her an incredulous look before shaking his head. "Ma'am, we're resupplying—"

"I am aware. Do you have the fuel and supplies to make it to Shuhon Island and the naval base there?" Azula asked, and the captain frowned.

Considering it for a few moments, the captain nodded. "If we resupplied fully there, then yes. Is that your order?"

"Yes. Make ready and set off for Shuhon Island within the hour. Resupply fully at the Shuhon naval base. Then set course for…?" Azula turned an expectant look on Mai.

"Gaoling. If not Gaoling, then Omashu," the taciturn girl supplied.

At Azula's nod, the captain turned to the other crewman. "Ensign, send word to have the men return and cancel our preparations. Finish loading what we can for the next hour, then prepare to cast off."

"Aye, cap'n," the man agreed, before hurrying off.

Azula turned and left the bridge after him, Mai and Ty Lee following. "Where are we staying?"

"I'll show you to our quarters. Ty Lee, go let June know," Mai instructed, and the shorter of the two nodded.

"Alright~, but she's gonna be annoyed…" Ty Lee hemmed, breaking off from the group and heading for the hatch leading outside.

Sending Mai a curious look, Azula asked, "Who is 'June' and why do we care if she's annoyed or not?"

Mai gave her an amused little smirk, before opening a seemingly random door in the ship. Azula wrinkled her nose at the small room occupied by two bunk beds. "I am not sleeping here—"

"Do you want to go after Zuko or not?" Mai asked, and Azula glared at her friend's backtalk.

After a moment, she realized Mai actually expected her to answer. Rolling her eyes, Azula nodded. "Yes."

"Then don't complain. This ship is small. It's only a corvette. But it's fast. It's a messenger ship. There isn't enough room on board to give everyone their own room. You're lucky this room has enough bunks for the four of us."

"Tch. Fine," Azula grumbled. "But I get the top bunk."

"June already claimed it," Mai shook her head, to Azula's annoyance. When the princess opened her mouth, Mai explained, "She's officially Zuko's bodyguard on paid retainer. She's our tracker. If Zuko isn't in Gaoling, she'll tell us where to go."

"And how is she going to do that?" Azula asked, arching an eyebrow.

Mai's smirk returned. "She has a shirshu."

Azula blinked, and her estimation of the supposed bodyguard, and her friends' reliability went up a bit. "Alright. Now. Tell me what's really going on."

Mai considered her for a moment before nodding. "You should sit down." Azula made to sit on the bed across from her friend, but Mai shook her head. "Not on something flammable."

Raising an eyebrow, Azula crossed her arms over her chest and sat on the floor, away from the bed. "I'm not going to like this, am I?"

"No." Taking a breath, Mai apparently decided to just rip the bandage right off. "Zuko got engaged to the princess of the Northern Water Tribe."

Azula felt her eye twitch, then wobbled as her body reminded her that she was still practically bone dry on chi. Biting down a curse, she glared at Mai. "Explain."

"It's fairly simple, as Zuko told it. He went to the nearest air temple from here, and when we showed up, he ran north to avoid us, thinking we wouldn't follow. There, he met Princess Yue. Zuko did something and wound up engaged to Yue. They left the north together and have been traveling together since. The last we knew, they were going to Gaoling. From there, Zuko wasn't sure where he wanted to go. He had a list. The other air temples, Kyoshi Island, Omashu, Ba Sing Se, the south pole, some library out in the desert."

Azula's hands clenched in her lap as she muttered, "I'm going to kill her. Then strangle him. He's my big brother, some Water Tribe hussy isn't good enough for him, princess or no!"

"Good luck with that." Azula looked up at Mai's tone. Raising an eyebrow that demanded an explanation, Mai shrugged. "She's a waterbender. A damn good one, according to Zuko." That infuriating smirk returned as she added, "Zuzu basically said she was like the Water Tribe version of you."

Azula opened her mouth, only to close it with a click of teeth and a frown as she considered that. For a moment, she almost asked if that meant that he had sought out a girl who reminded him of her.

"Right, something else I should mention," Mai continued, her tone entirely too casual to actually be casual. "Yue wants to have Zuko marry a girl from every nation. Preferably nobles, or as close as they can get. You know, for that whole Fire Lord thing when he comes back."

A shriek built in the back of Azula's throat at that and the room grew warmer as Azula finally hit her limit…

Only to fall over as the world swam for a moment, before going black.

Wandering Prince
Avatar the Last Airbender, Zuko SI
35
Commissioned by LurksTheMost.
Lightning popped on the water around us as we took in the island ahead of us, the boat below our feet rolling and swaying with every motion of the water as the storm hammered us with gale force winds and torrential rain. From the safety of the bridge, the island was a dark smudge on the horizon, occasionally backlit by lightning—blurry through the glass windows and metal slats covering them. The bridge, and the rest of the ship for that matter, was dark—no lights on outside or in any room with windows, no open flames. If it was this hard for us to spot the island, then there was no chance of anyone on the island spotting us, unless we made it easy for them, so we weren't.

"Nasty."

A hand squeezed my ass and I resisted the urge to jump. Reacting would just encourage them. Instead I reached back and eased the girl's hand away.

"You can barely see your nose in front of your face."

A new hand grabbed the other cheek and someone giggled. I pushed away the hand in question. Just ignore it—

"Man I sure wouldn't want to go out in that."

The other cheek, this time a full on squeeze. I flinched as the entire group of girls giggled and swatted the hand away.

"Yeah, you'd have to be dumb as a box of rocks to think that was a good idea."

I intercepted the hand coming from the right side and knocked it away, only for it to come right back in for a grab. I'm gonna kill 'em.

Suki turned an annoyed look on her sisters, her gaze shooting down behind me and up at them in silent warning. "What does that make us, then?"

"Rocks in a box!"

"So dumb!"

"This is gonna suuuck!"

"Hmm… But maybe we'll get a reward for it~."

I spun around as four hands decided to play simultaneous grabass. By the time I got turned around, the Kyoshi girls had their hands behind their backs, all of them wearing looks that said that butter wouldn't melt in their mouths. A fifth hand reached out and grabbed me and I looked down, in time to see Toph squeezing my crotch.

The little shitstirrer grinned up at me. "What? I didn't want to be left out!"

"Ah, youth," Uncle chuckled.

Giving it up as a lost cause, I eased Toph's hand off of me and turned to look at Uncle. "Wait for midnight?"

He considered for a moment, before shaking his head. "No. The storm may have passed by then. We'll make our move now, during the worst of it. Everyone will be reluctant to be outside." Glancing at Toph, he asked, "Is there a place to put in where we won't risk damaging the ship?"

"Yeah, the entire north side of the island is clear. The problem is, it's also all open ground. Anyone looking is going to see the ship."

"That is fine," Iroh nodded. Looking to the captain, he gave the order. "Take us in and beach the ship."

"Beach it, sir?" the captain asked, unsure.

Iroh nodded, before sending Toph a smile. "I'm sure getting the ship off the beach won't be a problem?"

The short girl chuckled. "I can do it."

"Good. Then let us go make final preparations," Iroh nodded. "Captain, let us know when we're about to make land."

"Yes, sir," the captain agreed, and we left the bridge.

The next twenty or so minutes were spent quietly preparing and making last minute checks. I spent the time making sure my swords were sharp as most of Suki's sisters divided themselves between doing the same, checking their fans, and ensuring their shields were ready. Suki herself began preparing a couple of bags with medical supplies, just in case. Toph, on the other hand, had joined Uncle in a game of pai sho, the pieces occasionally clicking on the board as they played and drank tea.

Finally, we heard the captain's voice come from the speaking tube mounted on the wall. "General Iroh, we will beach the ship in just a few moments."

"Thank you, captain," Iroh called as he stood and the rest of us followed suit.

We pulled our cloaks on as we made our way up to the deck, where the soldiers from the ship joined us. There was no need to waste time going over the plan again as the ship slowed and jerked beneath us as it hit the sand, its mass digging a furrow beneath it as it pushed partway up onto the beach. It came to a lurching stop and as a group, we jumped off and split up, rushing to take care of our tasks.

Uncle Iroh and his soldiers would secure the northern dock and our ship before splitting into three groups—one to stay behind on guard, the other two to secure the docks on the east and west side of the island. Toph and I would accompany the Kyoshi Warriors up the slope to take the village with the prisoners, with the Kyoshi girls splitting up and escorting them back either to our ship or the northern dock, where Uncle's men would see them into the buildings to wait for any other prisoners and wait out the storm. While they did that, Toph, Suki, and I would hurry to the far southern port and handle things there. Once all of the ports were secure, enemies dealt with, and prisoners freed and either on their way or hunkered down in place, the majority of our forces—aside from those left behind to guard the northern port and our ship—would meet in the center of the island before moving into the caldera to deal with the main pirate force.

The wet sand turned into a slog as we hurried up the beach and onto the trail. The dark and the rain would have made navigating anywhere except out in the open a nightmare. The fact that from the northern port up the slope to the village was all a big, open field was a mixed blessing. We could see and move quickly, but if the enemy looked outside, there was a chance they would see us coming.

We kept low in the grass, hurrying as fast as we could effectively move. The rustle of grass and splashing of our feet was covered by the sounds of the wind and rain, but dark shapes moving in the grass would still be visible if anyone on the higher elevation of the village looked down and happened to see us during a lightning flash.

Finally, we made it to the village proper and came to a stop just inside the line of grass. We all looked to Toph who took a moment to close her eyes, focusing on the ground through her feet and the stone sandals she wore.

"Five guards. Four playing something around a table in that building," she pointed to a newer stone structure on the outskirts of the village. "One in that one," she pointed to another building near the ones the prisoners were being kept in. "With a woman. Not sure if they're both guards or what, but they're fucking."

Nodding, Suki turned to her sisters and simply pointed at the building with the pair enjoying themselves. Then, she started moving up towards the other building. Toph and I moved to follow. Quietly, she asked, "How do we want to handle this?"

Thinking about it a minute, I grinned and looked to Toph. "Drop them underground, then push them back up one at a time."

Grinning, the short girl nodded. Concentrating, she stomped her foot and we faintly felt the ground rumble beneath our feet. "Done."

We moved into the room and Suki sighed. "It's almost too easy."

"Don't jinx us," I warned her, before nodding to Toph.

One of the men popped up, head and shoulders above ground level, and I crouched down in front of him. Pulling one of my swords, I asked, "Who's in charge here?"

"Fuck you! When we get out, I'm going to—urk!"

I slid my sword through his throat and motioned to Toph. He sank down and the next one rose up. "Who's in charge here?"

I only had to repeat the process once more before we found what passed for the commander in charge of the prisoners. I spent a few minutes questioning him about the interior of the island while Suki went to check on the others, taking Toph with her long enough to bring down the bars over the homes containing the prisoners. Unfortunately he didn't know much. With no further use for him, I finished him and the last guy off and Toph buried them when she returned.

"Well, that was a waste of time," she grumbled, and I nodded.

"They can't all be winners," I shrugged. "How are the prisoners?"

"Suki's explaining things and they're getting ready to run for the dock."

Nodding, I stepped out into the rain and quickly crossed over to the main building they were being kept in, just in time for the Kyoshi girls to lead them outside and direct them down towards the dock. Suki came over and joined us. "How'd it go?"

"They aren't thrilled about the Fire Nation being here, but at this point, they'll take whatever help they can get," she admitted. "Get anything?"

"Nothing of value," I shook my head.

The girl nodded. "It was worth a shot. Are you ready to hit the northern port?"

I glanced at Toph. "Let's go," she grinned, and we took off jogging onto the path heading south through the island interior. "You think I can actually fight someone this time?"

"Let's try to keep things quiet and stealthy as long as we can," I shook my head.

The shorter girl frowned, but nodded. "Yeah, I guess that's safer."

"Besides, you'll definitely get your chance soon. There's no way we're taking out the town in the center without things devolving into a fight."

Toph grinned. "Nice."

We fell silent after that, carefully moving along down the path towards our goal. Our only hiccup was when Toph quietly signaled and we moved off the path. Only a few seconds later, we spotted light coming from a firebender holding up a flame as a group of three men turned onto the path from side path and made their way towards us.

We heard the complaining before they reached us. "—but seriously, I don't see what we did to piss someone off enough to earn a night patrol in the rain!"

"There's no telling. But bitching about it won't make it go any faster. So why don't you shut up so we can get it over with in silence?"

"There's nobody out here! No one knows we're here! I don't see why we're even bothering with patrols! It's a waste of time."

"Because you were told to."

I carefully slipped my swords out of their sheath while Suki did the same beside me, and Toph produced a mace on the end of a long handle with her sand. We waited until they were past us before slipping out of the brush and creeping up behind them.

The first two were dead before they knew what was happening, as Suki took the head of the one on the left and I stabbed the middle one through the back, driving my swords up through his heart, putting out his flame. The one on the right had just enough time to turn and see the fates of his two friends before Toph's mace came down on his head. He went down with a nasty crack from his skull and neck—his skull deformed and leaking blood and brains as his body twitched. Toph quickly buried them beneath the path along with turning the dirt over to hide the blood and we hurried on our way.

We didn't see another patrol on the way to the southern docks, so were able to move relatively quickly. When we arrived, the lights were on in what passed for a bar but looked to have been repurposed from a storage building. We could hear men and women talking, drinking, and generally having themselves a good time. Toph took a few moments to use earthbending to scout for us and quickly recreated the village in miniature at our feet.

"Twenty or so in the bar. I don't think they're all pirates. Ones and twos in these buildings, seem like they're sleeping. A group of four in this one, all huddled on the floor. It looks kind of like a jail or something to my senses," she quickly reported.

"Split up?" Suki asked, and I nodded.

"Suki and I will take the surrounding houses. Toph, check the jail. If they're villagers, just leave them there for now. Then keep an eye on the situation and if you see trouble, take care of it. Meet up across from the bar."

"Got it," Toph agreed with a grin, and we split up to go about the gruesome work ahead of us.

Leaving my swords sheathed, I pulled my knife and used it to push up the simple latch holding the door locked from inside, then slipped into the first home. This was a small, remote island that survived off of fishing, so I wasn't at all surprised to see that the interior was a single room, with a cot at the far end from the door. Two people snored away in the cot and I quietly checked out the rest of the place to determine whether they were villagers or pirates.

Quickly finding their clothes, and the weapons that had been dropped on the floor beside them, I had my answer. A quick jab to the back of the first one's neck and a slash across the throat for the other had them taken care of, though I had to hold my hand over the man's mouth as he struggled and bled out. Feeling disgusted, I wiped my hand and knife off on the blanket and made my way to the next, reminding myself that these were pirates, slavers, and rapists and they deserved exactly what they got.

Though I'll admit that it's a bit different, looking into someone's eyes as they die, as opposed to burning them or killing them with a sword and moving on. Too personal.

Honestly, it was probably a good thing I didn't enjoy it. I took satisfaction in knowing they wouldn't be alive to hurt more people, but there was a difference between that and getting your rocks off on killing people.

Shaking my head to clear those thoughts, I hurried through checking the remaining houses. All of them were pretty much identical—houses barely worth being called huts, all holding a pirate or two that I left dead in their stolen beds.

When I finished, I made my way to the meeting point and found Suki waiting. She didn't look away from the bar as she asked, "Any trouble?"

"No. You?"

She shook her head, then glanced to the side. I turned to follow her gaze to find Toph hurrying up. "They're prisoners," she confirmed as soon as she was close enough for us to speak and not be overheard. "They saw me and if we don't get them out soon, they're going to make a racket."

"Great," I grumbled. "How do we want to do this?"

"I've had a look inside," Suki began, and I nodded, motioning for her to go on. "There are a few villagers—the cook, and some women who are serving drinks and acting as… entertainment." Pointing up near the top of the building, I spotted the outline of a window or something that had been closed from the rain. She continued, "I want to go in from the top, at the rear of the building."

"Gonna need a distraction so they don't hear it open," Toph pointed out, and Suki nodded, sending the shorter girl a smile.

"I'll leave that to you."

Toph grinned, turning to me with a look that practically begged me to agree. "Yes, yes. We can go in through the front door and make a scene. I'll leave that to you."

"Yes!" she cheered quietly. Turning back to Suki, she waved the Kyoshi girl towards the building. "Go!"

Chuckling, Suki slipped quietly but quickly across the muddy path that passed as a road and disappeared behind the building. Toph and I stood and made our way up to the front door. I held it open for her and she stepped in ahead of me. I made sure to close the door, then found the bar to keep it shut, dropping the big slab of wood into place as Toph threw back her hood and planted her hands on her hips. The bar had gone silent as everyone stared at Toph.

"Good news, losers! There's been a change in management! We're in charge, now! So for all you dirtbags, criminals, and pirate scum, this is your chance to throw down your weapons and surrender. If you do, you might get to live to see tomorrow! Any takers?" she demanded, shit eating grin on her face as she looked over the crowd.

Several of the pirates laughed, while many began pulling out weapons. One off towards a corner frowned and asked, "Hey wait, don't I know you from somewhere?"

That brought the pirates up short as they collectively paused, as Toph focused in on the guy in the corner. Studying him for a moment, she hummed. "Nope. Never met you."

"No hang on, I swear," he mumbled, thinking on it. "Was it in Ba Sing Se? No, uh… Gaoling?"

Toph's face lit up as she laughed. "Oh! No, I bet I know what it was! You went to the Earth Rumble, didn't you?"

"Yeah! That's it! I," he paused, then swallowed as he paled abruptly. "Oh. Oh shit! You're the Blind Bandit!"

Toph grinned. "Yup~."

The man abruptly stood and hurried for the back door, shaking his head. "Nope! Nu-uh. No way. I'm out!"

Toph took a single step forward, and across the room, a slab of rock jutted up in front of the back door. The man trying to flee whimpered as his shoulders slumped. A downward thrust of her palm had the ground opening up and swallowing the three waitresses I had counted, their yelps cut off as rock covered the ground above their heads.

That pushed the pirates into motion as those that hadn't already abruptly stood, drawing weapons. None of them appeared to be benders, so at least we didn't have to worry about that.

Movement from above drew my eye and I caught a flash of silver in the lantern light as Suki dropped from above, landing on the back of one of the pirates and drawing her sword across his throat, before pushing off and landing in a roll. Her katana swept out at ankle level and sent three more to the ground howling. Who I guessed was the chef lunged towards one of the pirates with a cleaver and buried it in the other man's neck with a roar.

The attention of some shifted towards the back and I stepped in, drawing and swinging in a single motion as I removed a man's hand holding his own sword. Toph jumped into the fray with a laugh, a big two-handed mace swing caving in a man's chest, then shifting to rock armor over her forearms as she deflected a swing at her head and returned with a punch that cracked the guy's jaw and snapped his head around at an unnatural angle, sending him to the ground as she moved on to the next.

My sword flashed out, catching arms, legs, and slicing throats where I found the opportunity as I worked my way through the crowd. Suki pushed in towards me and we found ourselves back to back, covering each other's blind spots as we moved, while Toph did her best to drive people towards us since, between her ridiculous strength and rock armor, she could just ignore the blows hammering down on her and then use her sand to bat people in our general direction.

The fight was short, brutal, and entirely one-sided.

When no one was left standing, Suki and I went about finishing off the men on the ground and making sure the rest were dead. Toph unblocked the door and brought the women back above ground. The three girls hurried over to the chef and clung to him as the man eyed us warily. One of the girls followed Suki with wide eyes.

"We don't have time to stick around, so listen. Are you natives to the island, or are you from somewhere else?" Toph asked as we worked.

"Aye. I'm from the island," the cook nodded, along with two of the girls.

"I, I'm from Kyoshi Island," the girl watching Suki answered. "Suki, is that you?"

The redhead looked up and sent her a smile. "Yep. We're all here. Don't worry, we're taking you all back home."

Toph glanced over at us before nodding. "Alright. Stay hunkered down here for the night. We've cleared out the pirates at the other ports and the village where they were keeping the prisoners. We'll come for you," she nodded to the Kyoshi girl, "when we get done clearing out the pirates in the middle of the island. Got it?"

The four all nodded as we opened up the door and Toph took a moment to bury the dead below the building. Then, we were back out in the rain. We took a moment to swing by the building they had been using as a prison and let Toph free them, telling them to head for the bar and stay there for now, before hurrying towards the meeting point.

As we went, Toph bumped my side. "That was fun."

"Fighting does get the blood pumping," Suki agreed from the other side, casting a sidelong look at Toph. "You handled yourself well back there." She turned a smile on me as well. "You too, Zuko."

"You weren't so bad yourself," I chuckled. "Nice moves with the ninja stuff. I'm a little scared to see what you girls can really do if you put your minds to it."

"Heh," Suki laughed quietly. "It's nice to be appreciated for your hard work, especially when we don't get many chances to really show off. I'll tell the girls you said so."

"Yeah, yeah," Toph nodded. "So~… Long boat ride to catch up to the other pirates when we're done here. It'll be hours."

"Time enough to get some food and catch some sleep before we deal with the other group, yeah," I agreed, turning an amused look on her as I had an idea of where she was going.

"You shouldn't just go to sleep straight after," Suki shook her head. "You should take some time to blow off some steam and remind yourself of the joys of life."

I held in a quiet snort. "Is that something Kyoshi passed down?"

"Yes, actually," Suki nodded, grinning. "It helps build team cohesion, you know."

Toph frowned, sending an annoyed look around me at Suki. "You're really just gonna go for it, huh?"

The redhead sent Toph a smile. "I'm just saying that the girls and I are going to spend the night enjoying ourselves, before we turn in. You're both welcome to join us."

The shorter girl sighed, before glancing at me. I sent her a smile. "I'll bring the pai sho set."

"We've got playing cards," Suki offered.

Narrowing her eyes, Toph asked, "No funny business?"

Suki sucked in a breath and winced. "I can't promise that," she shook her head. "Whatever you're thinking, they're going to want to do, and then some. Kyoshi help us if one of them brings alcohol."

"Surprised you're not playing some strip variant of whatever card game you've got in mind," I mused, and Suki's face lit up in a grin.

"Don't tell the others that, unless you want to lose all of your clothes," she warned, before eyeing me up and down, then blatantly doing the same for Toph. "On the other hand, could be fun…"

Toph… actually seemed to be considering it, as she eyed me up like a slab of beef. Meeting her gaze, she grinned. "Only if you're all playing," she finally offered.

"Deal," Suki agreed.

"Fine. I'll go along with it," I agreed. "On the condition that anyone caught cheating loses instantly and has to strip entirely."

Suki snorted a laugh. "That's not gonna go the way you think it is."

"Anyone caught cheating, huh?" Toph hummed, hiding her own grin.

Shaking my head, I asked, "How much further?"

Sighing, Toph paused and tilted her head. "Not much further to the tunnel leading to the interior. Most of the other groups are already there. Only the other Kyoshi Warriors are still on the way. They're close by. No one else around, so it's safe if you want to make some light."

Nodding, I created several orbs of chi and sent them floating around us, lighting the way and allowing us to speed up as we made for the tunnel. The other girls spotted the light and joined us just before we got to the tunnel, and I doused most of the lights to keep anyone on the other side from seeing us as we passed through, leaving just one to see by and keeping it hidden behind Toph's body, walking in front of us since she didn't actually need it to navigate.

"How did it go?" Suki asked, and the other four quickly caught her up.

We stepped out of the tunnel and spotted the lights of the fort town that had been erected shining in the middle of the caldera forest and I doused our light, leaving us in the dark—since up here, any source of light would absolutely stand out. I channeled my chi and the world lit up in infrared, allowing me to see, if not as well as with my normal sight. A very brief signal flashed from deeper in the forest. I flashed a small flame on the end of my finger in answer before putting it out.

"Uncle and his men are in position and waiting for us," I translated.

Toph took my hand. "The path is steep. I'll guide us down."

I took Suki's hand and the other girls did likewise, forming a line as we made our way down in the dark. When we got to the bottom of the caldera's slope, I conjured fire for everyone to see, since the trees provided cover and as long as we stayed on the path, then in theory anyone moving in this close should be one of their own patrols if we were spotted from a distance.

We found Uncle and the others waiting at the entrance to the tunnel we had made to get into the fort the first time we were here. Toph quickly opened the way and we made our way in out of the rain. Once the tunnel was sealed up behind us, I created more chi orbs as Toph expanded the surrounding area of the tunnel into an underground chamber, complete with chairs and table, so we could all stand and sit comfortably.

"How did everyone do?" Uncle asked as we sat.

"Ours went off without a hitch. There were only four people who weren't pirates in what passed for their bar. One of them is from Kyoshi, so we'll need to go back for her later. Toph freed a few prisoners who should be waiting with them," I explained, and he nodded. "What about you?"

"The east and west are secure. There were not many men guarding them, and few prisoners," Uncle answered.

"All the prisoners from the village have either been loaded on the ship or are waiting in the northern port," one of Suki's girls continued.

Smiling, Uncle nodded. "Then all that is left is this fort. Toph, if you would?"

The top of the stone table shifted, walls and buildings springing up from the surface. The buildings were all missing their roofs and inside, she had left pebbles to represent people. A few groups of pebbles moved slowly along the streets.

"There are people scattered all over the place. It's gonna be messy," she began, before tapping one of the larger buildings in the fort town—what I remembered was another bar and/or brothel. "Most of them are here, doing about what you'd expect. Lots of people who may or may not be pirates—men and women both, from what I can tell. More prisoners here," she pointed out another large building nearby.

"You're sure they are prisoners?" Uncle asked, and Toph nodded.

"Stone cell doors, so yeah. I think it's where they keep the prisoners when they're not working, but some of those cells are open and people are screwing, so…" she trailed off with a shrug as Uncle made a face.

"Mm." Uncle stroked his beard as he considered the map and the people on it. "There is a significant danger to the innocent. We will have to be cautious and act with discretion."

"We should hit the patrols first," Suki suggested, and Uncle nodded. "Leave that to me and my girls."

"You need me to go with?" Toph asked, and Suki shook her head.

"No, we'll be fine. As long as we know generally where they are and which direction they're going, we'll be able to find them quickly."

"And the prisoners?" I asked, and Uncle smiled.

"I'll leave that to the two of you," he nodded to me and Toph.

Looking to Toph, I asked, "Think you can do that trick you pulled at the port and stick the villagers underground while we handle the pirates?"

"The ones on the ground floor? Sure. Can't do anything about the ones on the next floor up."

"Why not pull everyone on the ground floor under? Or the entire building, if that's possible?" Suki asked, and Toph shook her head.

"I'm pretty sure there's another earthbender in there. If we're trying not to kill the prisoners, then pulling another earthbender underground where they might panic and accidentally squish everyone is a bad idea. I'm strong enough that I could overpower them normally, but if they panic, I might not be able to stop whatever they do in time."

"Yeah, let's avoid that," I agreed, earning a nod from Uncle.

"Okay. The top floor, then. That's where we start the assault. We'll move in and handle them after we deal with the patrols," Suki nodded. "We can clear the top floor quickly and quietly. No one will know we're there. That just leaves the buildings on the exterior and the lower floor of the brothel."

Uncle nodded, turning his gaze on me. "How do you think we should divide our forces, Zuko?"

I let out a quiet sigh. "Is now really the time for one of your lessons, Uncle?"

"Life is a lesson, nephew. You should always seek to learn more and work to sharpen your mind."

I rolled my eyes, but considered the options available. "The exterior is too spread out to cover without likely alerting someone to our presence, and if we try to go building by building with a small group, it's going to take forever. Time we don't really have, if we want to catch up with the fleet heading for Gaoling." At that, Uncle nodded, but remained silent. "Send the troops. Teams of two. Sweep for civilians. Rescue any they find, but if all they find are pirates, burn 'em. As for the brothel…"

I looked to Toph. "Everyone who isn't a pirate underground?" She nodded. "Can you move them out from under the building and bring them out in front of it?"

"Easy," Toph nodded.

I shifted my gaze to Suki. "Everyone upstairs cleared out?"

"We can sneak the villagers out the windows. We'll carry them if we have to. I can't guarantee it'll be quiet though."

"That's fine. I'll give you a distraction, but you're going to want to get clear fast. Let's go."

With that, we made our way down the tunnel and began our assault.

#4,411
Wandering Prince
Avatar the Last Airbender, Zuko SI
36
Commissioned by LurksTheMost.
I waited, watching from my position standing under the eaves of a building across the street from the brothel. In the brief light of a flash of lightning, I spotted figures on the surrounding rooves, jumping across the gap to land on the upper floor.

Alright, that's Suki and her girls moving into position. Time to go.

Pushing myself off the wall I'd been leaning against, I spotted a flare of red light go up before flashing, the sound of the pop lost in the crash of thunder.

And that's Uncle and his men starting their attack.

I slipped inside the front door, leaving a puddle from the water pouring off my cloak as I stood in the entrance and looked around for a moment, taking it all in. The sounds of laughter and conversation filled the air as pirates talked, drank, laughed, and gambled their money away. Off to the side, a younger woman sat with her eyes closed plucking at a pipa, while several more women moved through the crowd, serving drinks and food, and trying to dodge groping hands—while a few of them had been outright pulled into the pirates' laps and didn't look like they were enjoying themselves as they were being felt up.

No one paid attention to me as I pulled back my hood and made my way towards the bar, taking in the stock of liquor there. Humming to myself, I nodded as I came up with a plan to cause the maximum amount of chaos in the shortest amount of time. Taking a seat, I kept an eye on the crowd and waited for Toph to act.

"What'll it be?"

I glanced over to the bartender and shook my head. "Give me a minute to think on it."

He looked annoyed, but nodded and moved off. Somewhere above, I heard a faint thump, barely audible over the noise of the room. No one seemed to pay it any attention, even as another, louder thump sounded.

Come on already! Shit, we need some way to communicate. What I wouldn't give for a radio.

My thoughts were cut off as the ground rumbled and abruptly, the sounds of the pipa stopped as the woman holding it disappeared. The people nearest looked confused as they looked in the direction of where she had been. Then, one of the serving girls disappeared as a hole opened up beneath her, before closing again. Then another, and another. Sounds of alarm filled the room, which turned into panic when one of the men holding a woman disappeared.

"Alright, who's fucking around wi—ack!"

I hopped the bar, wrenching my knife out of the bartender's throat as I went and stabbing it down into the counter's surface. Grabbing a pair of glass bottles in both hands, I flung them into the crowd. One of them hit a man in the head and shattered, sending him to the floor. The other three hit tables and the floor. In the confusion, I had enough time to grab another four bottles and fling them before anyone could react, but by then, it was too late.

I followed up the barrage of booze with a fireball into the first man. Spilled liquor caught fire immediately as the fire quickly spread across the room and people began to yell. I flung a couple more bottles before one of the patrons rushed the bar. Grabbing another bottle, I smashed it into the side of his head and sent him tumbling to the floor, where the alcohol on his head and clothes quickly caught.

The ground rumbled and I moved, clearing the bar as a boulder came flying over the bar and smashed into the rack behind me. A jet of flame from under my feet sent me over the crowd and caught the wall and bar behind me. Pulling my dao blade, I split it down the middle, coming down between a pair of men and slashing with both. Guts spilled from one as I pulled the sword across his belly, while the other went down as the blade took him just below the knee.

A jet step powered leap launched me at the next, catching him across the neck with both swords in a scissoring motion that didn't quite have the reach for a full decapitation, sending his head tumbling back still attached to a flap of skin as he fell and turning him into a human Pez dispenser.

Bringing one sword around to intercept a blade, I twisted out of the way of a stab from behind and ducked below another bolder thrown at my head. Zeroing in on the earthbender, I launched myself out of the scrum at him, pulling on the fire burning around me and asserting control over it. Twisting in the air, fire roared at head and chest level, flowing out from my swords and sticking to people like napalm.

I caught the earthbender with a flying kick to the chest, but he was a big guy and rooted firmly to the ground with his feet encased in stone. So instead of launching him I kicked off, leaving his chest blackened as I spun just out of reach of a swing of his own massive sword. My feet had barely touched the ground when I shot forward, chi enhanced blades glowing cherry red cutting through the rock around his legs, then through the legs themselves, sending him to the ground with a scream of pain. Leaving him there, I spun through the crowd, dodging and blocking blows as I pulled on the fire again, moving towards the center of the building.

I dropped to one knee as I reached my target, taking a deep breath before bringing my swords down and sending fire spiraling through the room. Men burned as the shutters on the windows blasted inwards, ripped into the conflagration. I waited until the last of the pirates had fallen and the walls, ceiling, and floor were starting to slag. Standing, I took a few steps into the spinning mass of fire before pointing a sword straight up. Fire ripped through the ceiling, blasting a hole through the floor above, then through the roof as it roared up into the air above the brothel. The heat followed with it, boiling the rain and shrouding the area in steam as I quickly cooled the interior

There was nothing flammable left to burn on the lower level, leaving only scorched stone and ash surrounding a circle of stone untouched by the fire. I hurried out into the rain, gasping in great lungfuls of fresh, clean air as the rain poured over me. I let it wash off the worst of the smell, closing my eyes and turning my head up to enjoy it for a few moments as I flicked my swords off and put them back together, before slipping them back into their sheath.

I sensed several presences approaching and cracked an eye open to see Suki and the Kyoshi girls coming from one side and Toph from the other. Both were leading small groups of villagers—mostly women and girls, but a couple of younger men, and even some boys. I didn't like the implications, but it was something to deal with later.

"We good?" I asked, reaching up and scrubbing the water from my hair and face, before pulling my hood back up. A burst of heat flash dried my body, sending steam blowing off of me for just a moment.

"We're good," Toph nodded. "Feels like Uncle and his guys are wrapping things up. I don't sense anyone else."

"Soo… We're done?" One of the Kyoshi girls asked.

Another nodded. "Sounds like we're done."

"Back to the boat?" a third asked, earning nods from the others.

The fourth leered our direction, which prompted the others to do so as well. "Hey~. You guys want to play a game of cards when we get back?"

Suki rolled her eyes. "They've already agreed."

"Yes!"

"Thank Kyoshi!"

"I'll bring the snacks!"

"And I'll track down something to drink!"

"I'm gonna regret this," Toph grumbled, pressing herself into my side as we started down the street towards Uncle.

I put my arm around her shoulders as she leaned against me. "Probably."

"Don't worry, we'll take good care of you~" One of the Kyoshi girls promised, to sounds of agreement from the others.

Then, someone grabbed my ass. I sighed and followed the arm up to Suki, who studiously avoided looking at my face. Shrugging, I reached out and grabbed a handful of her own ass—to the sounds of catcalls from the others. I was pretty sure she blushed, but I couldn't be certain because of the face paint.
Toph grunted as she shoved, throwing her whole body into it. The sand below the ship heaved and slowly but surely pushed the ship back out to sea, turning the front around so it wouldn't have to reverse and could instead simply make a hard turn. Once we were sure it was clear, I picked her up and carried her as I jumped, jet stepping onto the deck of the ship as it got under way.

I took a look back at the island where we'd left the former prisoners, spotting the lights being put out in the building where we had left everyone. After getting all of the surviving villagers in one spot, I had taken an hour or so to heal what I could as the captain and the men got the ship ready to get under way.

While we were doing that, the Kyoshi girls and Toph had hurried back to the island's interior and looted what they could carry—which, with Toph's earthbending, was a lot. The pirates had collected a large amount of gold, jewels, and other things and the girls had come back with who even knew how much. And according to Suki, that was maybe a bit more than three quarters of the total haul. The rest, they had left for the village.

As for what they'd taken… Uncle, Suki, and I were all in agreement. It wasn't really ours to keep. At least, not all of it. We'd obviously be taking some of it for ourselves and the men as payment, but as for the rest, Uncle promised to see that it was evenly distributed among the villages the pirates had destroyed. There was just no way to ensure that everyone got the exact monetary amount that was taken from them, especially when you factored in destruction of property, deaths, bodily harm, rapes, and everything else.

I wished him luck in figuring out that mess and washed my hands of it entirely. I was sure Uncle would do the best he could and that was good enough for me.

Stepping in out of the rain, I set Toph down and dried us off. "What do you think? Shower before we join the others?"

"They're definitely already getting cleaned up," Toph nodded, before grinning at me. "We could save time and water by showering together."

Chuckling, I nodded. "Sure. Let's go. No hanky panky, though."

"Not even a little?" she asked, and seeing her cute pout, I rolled my eyes.

"Maybe a little," I agreed, and the short girl laughed, before grabbing my hand and dragging me off towards our quarters.

Despite getting a little handsy, and a bit of grinding here and there, we managed to get cleaned up and dry without incident—somehow. Toph didn't bother with anything more than a bath robe, while I pulled on a set of pants and a top. As soon as we were dressed, we made our way to Suki and the girls' cabin and knocked.

One of the Kyoshi girls answered and grinned upon seeing us. "They're here!" she called, before grabbing both of us by the hand and pulling us inside.

I immediately realized we had perhaps walked into a trap as the girls, in various states of undress, eyed us up like a pack of hungry wolves—not just me, but Toph as well. I felt a little bit like that one meme of the person on the couch…

Suki patted the seat next to her and I dropped into it, Toph sitting on my other side as the girls piled in around the table. All of them were bare faced and smiling happily. One of them carried a stone tray over—likely made by Toph—and set it down in the middle of the small table between us. Another opened up the bag she carried and pulled out several unmarked bottles of alcohol—one of which was obviously sake, but from the coloration I thought one of the others might be rum, while I wasn't sure about the last one.

"If our resident firebender wouldn't mind?" the girl with the tray pushed it forward and I had a look inside. It was covered in shishkebabs, with half of them being chicken and the other half vegetables. All of them were covered in some kind of sauce that smelled strongly of alcohol and fruit.

"Sure," I agreed, and started picking them up to cook one by one as someone passed out stone plates and cups, and the girls poured drinks.

Beside me, Toph took a sip of whatever she had been handed and let out a quiet hiss. "Blech. That has to be the cheapest sake I've ever had the misfortune of tasting."

"Oh yeah?" Suki asked, sending Toph an amused look as she took a sip of her own. "Expensive tastes?"

"No surprise, she's a Beifong."

"Maybe we should get her to supply the booze next time!"

Toph rolled her eyes. "Not really. But you have to be able to tell the difference. My parents hired a tutor just for alcohol tasting, so I wouldn't embarrass my future husband," she grumbled. A smirk pulled at her lips as she leaned back, openly scratched at her crotch, and belched.

I sighed, sending her a look that said I knew she was just being obnoxious and gross on purpose. "Really?"

"You embarrassed yet?" she asked, wagging her eyebrows before slugging down the apparently crappy sake.

"We're not in public, so no." She got a look in her eyes at that and I glared at her. "Don't you dare."

"Oh, I'm gonna," the brat grinned, and I realized I had only succeeded in egging her on.

"If you do it, you get a spanking," I warned.

Toph leered. "Well now I'm definitely doing it~."

The Kyoshi girls shared a grin before one of them quietly said, "One of us."

That set the rest off as they took up the chant.

"One of us!"

"One of us!"

"One of us!"

"Girls," Suki groaned, blushing as she palmed her face. "Can you try not to scare them away?"

They considered it for a moment, before one grinned. "Sure Suki."

"Yeah, we haven't even gotten to the good part yet."

"Zuko~! You haven't touched your drink!"

"Yeah, drink up!"

I sent them an amused look as I finished cooking another skewer and put it on a plate. "Somehow, I have this sneaking suspicion that if I don't keep my wits about me, my virtue might just be in danger."

"From us? How could you think that, Zuko?!"

"We would never get you and Toph drunk and take advantage of the two of you!"

"Yeah, we'll do it while you're sober."

"It's Suki you have to watch out for!"

I glanced over at Suki, who rolled her eyes. Nodding, I started on another skewer. "Yeah, I can see who the real danger is here."

"Kyoshi give me strength," Suki sighed quietly, before sending a light glare my way. "And you should really stop encouraging them."

"Eh, I'm sure it'll be fine," I sent her a smile, as the other girls tittered, sharing mischievous looks I probably wasn't meant to see.

Soon enough, the food was cooked and we dug in. As we ate, I asked, "So, what was life like on Kyoshi Island, growing up?"

"It was so boring~!" one of the girls whined.

"All Suki wanted to do was train!" another nodded.

"Train, and go on adventures," the third pointed out. "It was great."

The last one sighed, sounding a bit wistful. "It just hasn't quite been the same without Mingxia."

I raised an eyebrow, but it was Toph who asked, "A friend?"

"A sister," Suki murmured. "She didn't agree with Oyaji's isolationist policy. She felt that the island was slowly dying because of it. A famine brought everything to a head. Mingxia wanted to use the situation to convince the other village heads to pressure Oyaji to open the island up more to outsiders and trade. I disagreed. We all worked together to go out and gather wild edible plants to help with the situation. It worked long enough to get the island back on our feet.
